title: Robinhood Chain's real-world assets jump fivefold as tokenized stocks start trading in bigger size
full_text:
Robinhood Chain's real-world assets jump fivefold as tokenized stocks start trading in bigger size
The chain built to put equities onchain has tripled in size since mid-July, and a dozen tokenized stocks are now each clearing $500,000 a day. Real-world assets are growing fast, though memecoins and stablecoins still dominate the chain.
- Tokenized real-world assets on Robinhood Chain have surged to about $70 million in value, a roughly fivefold increase in less than two weeks, as tokenized equities begin trading at scale.
- A dozen tokenized stocks, led by GameStop, Nvidia and SpaceX, are now each clearing at least $500,000 in daily volume, with several surpassing $1 million.
- Despite the growth in tokenized equities and a tripling of total value locked to about $312 million, stablecoins and memecoin trading still dominate Robinhood Chain’s activity, making the shift toward real-world assets significant but still partial.
When Robinhood Chain first launched, its activity was dominated by speculative memecoin trading rather than the original reason it was built — tokenization.
However, the momentum has finally started to shift, less than two weeks later.
Real-world assets now carry an active market value of about $70 million, according to DefiLlama, a roughly fivefold jump from the low tens of millions of dollars, which was a small slice of the network at just 4%, while memecoins and stablecoins accounted for most of the activity. The tokenized equities for which the chain was designed are finally trading in larger sizes.
A tokenized GameStop share is doing $26.6 million in daily volume on the exchange, with Nvidia at $14 million and SpaceX at $6.4 million close behind. Twelve Robinhood-based tokenized stocks are now clearing more than $500,000 a day, with five above $1 million.
In its earliest days, the chain's busiest market was CASHCAT, a memecoin built around Robinhood's abandoned original name. The company was briefly "CashCat" before its founders settled on Robinhood. The token, which Robinhood has no part in, spiked more than 1,700% after CEO Vlad Tenev followed its account, then fell. It is now down about 75% from its peak, while a number of real equities trades in its place.
Total value locked has roughly tripled since mid-July to about $312 million, according to DefiLlama, and Robinhood Chain is now clearing more than $600 million in daily decentralized-exchange volume, putting it among the more active networks in crypto.
Its transaction count has also drawn attention, with more than 138 million in 30 days, per Token Terminal. But the chain's most-traded tokens are still overwhelmingly memecoins.
On DEX Screener, the top of Robinhood Chain's trending list is filled with tokens like “Hoodrat,” “Vladhood” and “Swole Doge,” not the tokenized equities the network was built for, which trade on Uniswap but rank well down the volume rankings.
The tokenized stocks generate roughly $55 million in daily volume, under a tenth of the chain's nearly $600 million in total DEX trading, the data shows. The rest is dominated by memecoins.
Stablecoins remain the single largest presence on the chain, with a combined market value in the hundreds of millions of dollars, and memecoins, such as the Robinhood mascot-themed CASHCAT, that defined the chain's first weeks, are still active and heavily traded.
The critique three weeks ago was that Robinhood had built expensive infrastructure and attracted only speculation, with little sign that the tokenized-stock business it pitched would materialize.
That business is now materializing, in the form of tens of millions of dollars in real-world assets and a dozen equities trading in real size. However, it remains small compared to the chain’s stablecoin and memecoin ecosystems, and it will need to keep growing to meet Robinhood’s original vision for tokenization.
But as the data indicates, the tokenized stock activity is moving toward the pitch rather than away from it as the company builds towards bringing millions of its retail customers onchain.

title: Dango’s perp DEX taps out nearly 4 months after launch
summary: Dango will close its network on Aug. 13, joining BitMEX, Odos and Satori Finance in a wave of recent crypto shutdowns.
full_text:
Dango’s perp DEX taps out nearly 4 months after launch
Dango will close its network on Aug. 13, joining BitMEX, Odos and Satori Finance in a wave of recent crypto shutdowns.
Layer-1 blockchain Dango will wind down operations by halting trading on its perpetual decentralized exchange (DEX) on Wednesday and shutting down its network on Aug. 13.
“Despite our best effort, various reasons have led us to conclude there is no viable path to a lasting commercial success,” Dango said in a Friday X announcement.
Dango founder Larry Liu added that the team faced cash shortages, legal challenges that slowed momentum, the loss of team members, and broader market conditions.
Dango launched its mainnet in January after raising $3.6 million in a 2024 seed round led by Hack VC and Lemniscap. It rolled out its perpetual DEX in April, only to suffer a roughly $410,000 exploit days after launch. The attacker later returned the funds in exchange for a bug bounty.
Related: BitMEX hit with 623 BTC lawsuit on day it announces shutdown
Dango’s open interest dwarfed by Hyperliquid, Aster
According to DefiLlama, Dango’s total value locked fell from a peak of roughly $4.5 million in early May to about $1.6 million before the announcement.
The perp DEX market is increasingly competitive and dominated by a handful of platforms.
Hyperliquid held more than $11 billion in open interest on Saturday, which represents the value of outstanding perpetual futures contracts that haven’t been closed.
Perp DEX ranking by open interest. Source: DefiLlama
Only Aster and Variational also hold more than $1 billion in open interest. Dango held just under $391,000 in open interest.
CoinGecko said in its second quarter industry report that Hyperliquid became the second-largest perpetual exchange by open interest on July 1, behind only Binance.
A summer of crypto shutdowns
Dango’s shutdown adds to a growing list of crypto platform closures in July, including 11-year-old perpetual futures pioneer BitMEX.
Restructuring adviser Roshan Dharia told Cointelegraph that BitMEX’s shutdown reflects structural pressures facing mid-sized centralized exchanges, where liquidity has increasingly concentrated among the industry’s largest players and regulatory compliance costs continue to rise.
“The top five platforms now control an estimated 80% of global spot volume, leaving mid-tier and regional exchanges with shrinking margins and no viable path to scale,” Dharia said.
Other recent closures include DEX aggregator Odos Protocol and perp DEX Satori Finance.

title: Cricut Explore 5 vs. Siser Romeo: Choosing the Right Smart Cutting Machine (2026)
summary: Friendly hobby machine or serious production tool? Here’s how to know which one is for you.
full_text:
Smart cutting machines are a black hole, and I say that as someone who fell in. I’ve dabbled with Cricut products, but it wasn’t until I started reviewing them for work that these cutting machines became a true obsession. These days, I spend weekends thrifting for blanks and experimenting with patchwork appliqué, and I even caved and bought a secondhand Brother sewing machine. My home office, which once screamed “corporate remote worker,” is now overrun with glitter vinyl and who knows how many types of scissors (all for different purposes, of course).
In This Story
All of which to say, I was an easy target when Cricut and Siser both landed new, smart cutting machines on my desk. I quickly realized that comparing them to each other wasn’t particularly useful. Yes, they both cut materials like vinyl and cardstock, but they solve different problems and are for different consumers. Cricut’s latest model, the Explore 5, costs $199 for the machine alone (or $250 for the bundle I tested with mats, tools, and vinyl) and is designed for the more casual crafter making things like bookmarks, banners, and the occasional T-shirt. The Siser Romeo ($600 as tested), on the other hand, is built for someone who might pump out 50 graphic tees before lunch.
Siser has always been upfront about this. It’s not really trying to compete with a machine like the Explore 5. So instead of forcing a winner-take-all comparison, I over several weeks cut layered cardstock bookmarks, HTV hoodies, vinyl-decaled cups for my brother-in-law’s 40th birthday, and even bonded cotton appliqué pieces on both machines (disclaimer: I had to buy new, aftermarket blades for this).
My goal wasn’t to crown a winner but to evaluate where the tipping point was. When do you outgrow a hobby cutter? More specifically, when is it worth trading the Cricut Explore 5’s simplicity for the Siser Romeo’s added control?
Cricut Explore 5
If you’re casually personalizing things on the fly, or making cards or decals, the Explore 5 is your machine. More than the machine itself, though, my favorite part of Cricut is the whole ecosystem. The Design Space software is packed with user-created projects, and I could easily lose track of time finding designers I liked, then browsing and bookmarking everything they’ve made. You can start with one of those templates, customize it to your liking, and have it ready to cut in a matter of minutes. Design Space holds your hand through every single step, and the learning curve is shallow.
The Explore 5 is more of a background worker. Its new Load and Go system makes the act of cutting super simple: You put your material on the mat (which isn’t even needed if you’re using Cricut’s Smart Vinyl), feed it into the machine, and press the flashing Go button—the machine takes it from there. Combined with Design Space’s step-by-step prompts, it’s about as close to plug-and-play as a cutting machine gets.
At just under 20 inches wide, the Explore 5 doesn’t require a dedicated crafting studio space or permanent workstation. Mine lived happily on the corner of my desk for weeks, ready whenever inspiration struck. I also appreciated the clamshell-style opening, which keeps the blade and interior protected from dust and stray threads that inevitably exist in a busy craft space, and you can fold it closed when you’re done.
This machine isn’t flawless. During testing, I ran into inconsistent cuts on cardstock projects even with a fresh sticky mat. My first real project on the machine, an intricate floral bookmark, came out rough enough that I questioned whether paper crafting was for me. Sharpening the blade with a ball of foil and a swipe of rubbing alcohol helped, but I still had to break out an X-Acto knife to clean up some edges.
I’ve also had the occasional Bluetooth drop between finishing a design in Design Space and sending it to the machine—luckily never midcut, but it has happened often enough that I’ve gotten into the habit of starting projects from the app on my phone as a workaround. If you get stuck, though, help is never far off. Since Cricut is such an established brand, TikTok and YouTube probably have a creator who has solved your exact problem.
Siser Romeo
Whether you’re cutting heat-transfer vinyl in large volumes, running a business, or filling repeat orders, the Romeo is built for a completely different workflow than the Explore 5. At more than twice its size, it’s designed less for the spontaneous weekend project and more for keeping production moving.
It all starts with the hardware. Thanks to the adjustable pinch rollers, the Romeo doesn’t require a cutting mat for most materials, and instead of trimming vinyl into smaller pieces, you can feed and roll it through the back of the machine. A tiling feature also maximizes material by automatically filling the available space with duplicate designs, which is helpful when you’re cutting a dozen identical decals or shirt transfers.
The Romeo’s biggest strength is the amount of control that you as the user have over the machine. Its built-in registration camera automatically reads print-and-cut registration marks, and once you’ve lined up a project for cutting, you can save its settings as a preset directly on the machine. That kind of repeatability starts to matter when you’re making the same project over and over.
I also grew to appreciate being able to tweak cut settings directly from the Romeo’s display. If a cut wasn’t going deep enough, I could bump up the force or slow the cutting speed without touching my computer. I usually relied on the settings the machine defaulted to, but having those controls in front of me made it easier to fine-tune projects.
Leonardo, Siser’s dedicated software, gives you a lot more granular control than Cricut Design Space, but it doesn’t walk you through it and assumes you’re comfortable tweaking fonts, applying effects, separating layers, and adjusting cut settings. I often found myself making designs in Canva (where I’m faster and more comfortable), and then importing those files into Leonardo. (The good news: The Siser folks told me a Canva integration is on the way!)
More than once, Leonardo threw up a generic error pop-up with no explanation of how to fix the problem. You’re forced to dismiss the message before doing anything else, which feels like hitting a dead end before trying to troubleshoot yourself or looking up the error code in Leonardo.
Connectivity, luckily, is super simple and seamless. The Romeo connects to your computer over Wi-Fi instead of Bluetooth, which sounds like a minor detail until you’ve wrestled with the quirks that Bluetooth can sometimes pose (looking at you, Design Space). During my testing of the Explore 5, I’d occasionally lose my Bluetooth connection, requiring me to disconnect the machine from my computer, reconnect, and try again. I’m not sure if that’s a Design Space issue or my laptop juggling too many Bluetooth devices, but it can be a headache. Through my testing, I never once had the Romeo machine unexpectedly disconnect.
There’s no getting around it: The Romeo is big—it’s got twice the cutting width of the Explore 5. It’s not the type of machine that sits easily on a closet shelf when you’re not using it. Most people will want to dedicate a table to it. That’s not necessarily a downside, but it’s intended to exist like a permanent fixture in your workspace. (And remember to account for clearance behind the machine, since materials feed through the rear!). But it is sturdy and built well; it never shifted on the table while cutting, there was very little vibration, the carriage moved seamlessly with no rattles, and nothing flexed or creaked.
Its open design is another trade-off. Unlike the Explore 5, which folds up, everything stays exposed on the Romeo. I haven’t noticed any buildup yet, but I do worry about pet hair and dust getting into the internals, and it’s something that I’ll keep an eye on over time.

title: 3 Clever Things You Can Do With an Old Amazon Kindle
summary: These e-readers are more useful in their old age than you might think.
full_text:
The best Amazon Kindles are reliably good at their main job: displaying ebooks in a crisp, easy-on-the-eye format. But Kindle e-readers are actually more versatile than you might imagine.
If you’ve just upgraded to a new Kindle and are looking for something to do with your old one, or if you’re simply interested in seeing how hackable these e-readers are, we’ve got three projects for you to attempt.
These projects vary in terms of difficulty and the amoung of time and effort you’re going to have to invest, but full instructions for all of them are available online, so you can follow the steps on your own Kindle.
Turn Your Kindle Into a Spotify Controller
Part of the appeal of Spotify is that it can work across so many different devices and connect to so many other services. There are lots of ways to use Spotify, and that includes through your Kindle. All you need to do is supply your Spotify credentials, and then make sure your Kindle is on the same Wi-Fi network as the other device you’re using to play your music, podcasts, or audiobooks.
This is made possible through Kindlify.co. Open the site in the Kindle’s built-in web browser, then tap Connect Spotify to log in. Once that’s done, you should see details of whatever you’re currently playing in Spotify—though you will need to use another device to choose something from your library. There’s more discussion about this hack on Reddit, which is where I found it.
It all works through the magic of Spotify Connect, which you may already have come across. This feature lets you play something on your laptop and then control playback from your phone, for example, or vice versa. You can also use the feature to manage playback through compatible smart speakers.
Bear in mind that you’re not actually storing any music on your Kindle or running an official Spotify app. This hack is just a way to connect to your Spotify account and control whatever’s being played through it, from your Kindle. You can skip forward and backward, and pause and resume playback, all from the e-reader.
Turn Your Kindle Into a Smart Home Display
Another way to repurpose a Kindle and its E-Ink screen is to turn it into a smart display that pulls in all kinds of data from other services. You can use the e-reader to show a variety of information related to your devices, including weather forecasts, calendar information, and your to-do lists.
This is just about the most involved of the projects featured here, and you need to do everything from setting up a custom website to cutting out a custom-made frame for your Kindle. Developer Matt Healy, who originally put all this together, has diligently provided instructions online.
It’s the sort of project you can try if you want to learn more about hardware hacking, coding, the inner workings of Kindles, and how various apps and services talk to one another. By the time you’ve finished, you may well have some ideas about similar hacks of your own you could attempt.
The information you display is entirely up to you, but it will need to come from platforms that allow third-party connections. You can see from the scripts supplied by Matt Healy that he’s managed to pull in real time information from weather services, calendars, and even status reports for upcoming deliveries.
Turn Your Kindle Into a Literary Clock
Finally, you can also consider turning your Kindle into a literary clock. This hack keeps the e-book theme but repurposes the device into a display you can glance at any time you want to know what time it is, with each minute represented by a different quote from a book that mentions that particular time.
As with the smart home display, this requires a significant amount of work in terms of coding and getting everything set up, but again, there are full instructions online, so you can tackle it yourself. You can fashion a stand or frame for the clock, but it’s not essential if you don’t mind the original look of the e-reader clock.
One of the bigger steps you have to work through here is getting all the images in place. There are 1,440 minutes in each day, and this project will give you a static picture with a literary quote for each one of them. The good news is that all the images and associated scripts have already been prepared, so you don't have to create or source them yourself.
A nice touch is that you don’t get to see the name of the book or the author on the time quote, so the clock doubles as a sort of literary quiz. See if you know—or can remember—where each line comes from when you see it. You can then reveal each answer with a press on the Kindle’s screen.

title: Why Leatherology Makes Some of the Best Totes for Work (2026)
summary: I packed these Leatherology totes with laptops, chargers, and everything else my workday demands. Months later, they’re still the bags I keep reaching for.
full_text:
My tote bag is more a mobile workstation than a carrier. On any given day, it’s hauling a 16-inch laptop, noise-canceling headphones, chargers, my daily planner, a water bottle, and whatever gadgets I’m testing that week. Plenty of leather totes look beautiful on day one, but far fewer are designed to hold up against the reality of transporting thousands of dollars’ worth of tech every single day.
That’s why Leatherology surprised me.
After months of rotating between the Mia Horizontal Tote, Transit Travel Tote, and Large Zippered Downtown Tote, I found myself thinking less about the leather—though it’s undeniably excellent—and more about how each bag has been intentionally designed to fit specific workflows.
But the first thing you notice, of course, is that leather. Leatherology uses semi-aniline, drum-dyed pebbled leather that is soft and supple, making it feel broken in from day one without being overly delicate.
The hardware is clean, the branding is subtle, and the totes don’t feel ostentatious, which I appreciate. These bags look expensive because the quality of the materials and craftsmanship speak for themselves, not because there’s a flashy logo plastered on them. And if you want something more personal, every model can be monogrammed.
As a tech reviewer, though, I find that aesthetics go only so far. What impressed me most about these bags is their functionality, which is something I can’t say about many luxury bags. The straps remained comfortable even when I loaded the bags with bulky gear. The interiors are well-organized, preventing cables and accessories from getting lost in a single, cavernous compartment, yet they don’t feel over-engineered. Each bag is sturdy and secure enough to protect your valuables.
Built Better Than It Looks
The Mia Horizontal Tote ($330) is the most relaxed of the three and has become my go-to bag for the weekend. Its wider silhouette is ideal for farmers market runs, shopping trips, or afternoons working from a coffee shop when I don’t need my entire desk setup. My Kindle, headphones, a sweater, and small essentials all fit comfortably with room to spare. Two interior slip pockets kept accessories within reach, while the removable leather pouch became my designated home for my card holder and lip balm. The magnetic closure allows for easy access during everyday errands, but because it lacks a dedicated laptop sleeve or zippered top, I wouldn’t use it as a work bag for my commutes.
That’s where the Transit Tote ($465) comes in. This is the bag that feels purpose-built for work trips, where a personal item often doubles as your office. It features two exterior pockets, nine interior pockets, two zippered compartments, and a padded laptop sleeve that fits up to a 16-inch laptop. I could separate chargers, travel documents, and toiletries into designated, well-organized spaces. A hidden trolley sleeve slides over rolling luggage, and the zippered top adds an extra layer of security at airports. Between the short leather handles and longer shoulder straps, it’s also comfortable to carry through terminals without constantly shifting your grip. Plus, it feels much more heavy-duty than the Mia Horizontal, whose straps I sometimes worry might give out when the bag is overpacked. There’s also a foldable bottom gusset with a removable support panel that helps the bag maintain its structured silhouette. During my testing, it fit comfortably under an airline seat, but it’s always worth confirming measurements with your specific aircraft.
Still, as much as I liked the Transit, the Large Zippered Downtown Tote ($285) became my favorite. It’s the Goldilocks bag of the lineup, the sweet spot between elegance and utility, and better than almost any leather tote I’ve carried. It’s large enough to accommodate my remote work setup without feeling like it might tear, which makes it the bag I reach for most days. Even fully loaded, the structured silhouette holds its shape, giving it a polished appearance that transitions from office meetings to dinner afterward. It adds just enough personality without limiting what I could wear with it, and the recycled polyester and cotton twill lining feels durable enough to withstand years of commuting.
Despite its generous interior, it doesn’t turn into a black hole thanks to two open pockets, a zippered interior pocket, and a removable leather pouch for smaller items. The full-length zipper offers the kind of security I want when carrying a laptop. Leatherology also offers an optional water-resistant insert with insulated and mesh compartments, making the tote even more adaptable for parents, photographers, or anyone who wants additional organization. I don’t have one at the moment, but I would consider purchasing a bag insert to help protect the interior, which could be difficult to clean if it stains.
A Little Extra TLC
At the end of the day, these are also premium leather bags, and while they’re built to be worn, they still require care and maintenance. You’ll want to spot-treat the lining with a baby wipe or a damp cloth to help minimize stains. You should condition the bag every six months or so with an all-natural leather conditioner to help preserve the leather’s texture. When storing the bag, it’s best to stuff it with tissue paper or soft fabric to maintain its shape; for extra protection, I also keep mine in the provided dust bag. And lastly, you don’t want the bag to get wet, so I’d avoid wearing it on rainy days or in extreme weather. If it does get wet, wipe it dry as soon as possible.
Leatherology’s appeal isn’t about chasing trends or projecting status. Instead, it’s about recognizing how modern professionals move through their day. We commute between home and the office, work from coffee shops, catch flights, and expect one bag to transition seamlessly across it all. These totes meet that reality with thoughtful organization and a timeless design built to last. In a zeitgeist where our bags have become extensions of ourselves and our workspaces, that’s exactly what I want.

title: The OpenAI Models That Hacked Hugging Face Were ‘Active on the Internet’ for Days
summary: Plus: Russian hackers are trying to steal US nuclear scientists’ emails, the State Department bans known scammers from entering the United States, and more.
full_text:
Two of OpenAI’s cybersecurity-focused models broke out of a testing sandbox this week and went on to hack the AI research platform Hugging Face in an effort to solve a security benchmark test. Plus, researchers this week shed light on newly identified malware that is capitalizing on blind spots in AI software development infrastructure to grab logins and other sensitive data, even causing destruction to victims’ target files and systems.
Looking at the more traditional security nightmare of embedded devices, researchers this week shed light on a car alarm that was installed in vehicles across the US—and that is still silently lurking with a flaw that leaves millions of vehicles vulnerable to hacking and paralysis. There’s a patch available, and WIRED has details on how to check whether your car may have been exposed.
US states have worked to bar ICE agents from wearing masks, but Trump administration lawyers are pushing back, claiming that anti-mask laws endanger agents. Their public evidence is incredibly thin, though. Meanwhile, a WIRED investigation revealed that Madison Square Garden briefly disabled its sprawling, controversial surveillance system for Taylor Swift’s rehearsal dinner on July 2. And the ACLU is equipping lawyers in Massachusetts with a new toolkit to expose state surveillance technologies used for building criminal cases—shedding light on everything from face recognition tools to AI-written police reports.
Analysis of satellite images of Myanmar shows dozens of alleged scam compounds cropping up in recent months following a purported crackdown on the criminal operations in the region. Plus, a novel analysis of apps marketed to US service members found that more than one in eight contained foreign code, including code developed by US adversaries like Russia and China.
And there’s more. Each week, we round up the security and privacy news we didn’t cover in depth ourselves. Click the headlines to read the full stories. And stay safe out there.
The OpenAI Models’ Hack of Hugging Face Comes Into Focus
Additional details on the Hugging Face breach from The Wall Street Journal include findings that OpenAI’s models seem to have escaped containment and were apparently “active on the internet for several days before anyone stopped them.” The models, which had been tasked with completing a cybersecurity benchmarking test, were essentially attempting to cheat by simply accessing the solutions on Hugging Face’s infrastructure. Hugging Face cofounder and chief science officer Thomas Wolf says that before the company had any idea that it had been hacked by OpenAI models, he and his colleagues knew something about the breach was unusual because the attackers were simply tapping cybersecurity datasets rather than grabbing sensitive or potentially valuable data. He adds that the company eventually brought the situation under control with the help of an open-weight Chinese AI model that lacked the guardrails other models place on cybersecurity-related tasks.
Russian Operatives Go After Emails of US Nuclear Scientists and Defense Contractors
US and allied intelligence agencies warned on Thursday that a Russian state-backed hacking group had targeted nuclear scientists, defense contractors, and government employees in a year-long cyberespionage campaign aimed at stealing sensitive information from Western institutions.
To compromise their targets, the Russian hacking group known as Laundry Bear and Void Blizzard exploited a previously unknown flaw in Zimbra, an email platform used by governments and other organizations. According to security firm Proofpoint, simply viewing or previewing a malicious message in a vulnerable version of Zimbra’s webmail client could cause hidden code in the email to run, a technique the firm described as a “half-click” exploit. The flaw was exploited as early as July 2025, months before it was patched that November.
Once activated, the malicious code could copy the previous 90 days of a victim’s email, collect an organization’s address directory, steal saved passwords and two-factor authentication codes, and create a new application password that allowed the hackers to maintain access to the account.
The hackers targeted organizations involved in nuclear research, energy, and the defense industries, as well as government agencies, universities, law enforcement organizations, media outlets, and technology companies.
US Restricts Visas for Scammers
The State Department said on Thursday that it would restrict visas for foreign cybercriminals involved in scams and extortion, expanding the Trump administration’s campaign against criminal networks that target Americans from overseas. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the restrictions could apply both to people who carry out the crimes and, in some cases, their immediate family members.
Rubio authorized the restrictions under a 1952 immigration law that allows the US government to deny entry to people whose presence could have serious consequences for American foreign policy. The administration has used the same authority to restrict visas targeting members of groups it labels far-left extremists, raising concerns that lawful protesters or political opponents could be swept in.
The Trump administration has increasingly focused on large scam operations that use romance schemes, fraudulent cryptocurrency investments, and sexual blackmail to steal money or coerce victims. Many of the networks operate outside the US, making arrests and prosecutions difficult. In June, the Justice Department seized infrastructure connected to subsidiaries of the Huione Group, a Cambodian conglomerate that officials have linked to a major marketplace used by cybercriminals.
US Says Iran-Backed Hackers Are Targeting American Water and Energy Suppliers—Again
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, FBI, NSA, and Department of Energy warned on Wednesday that hackers linked to the Iranian government are actively targeting American water and energy providers. The attacks have targeted programmable logic controllers (PLCs), on internet-connected infrastructure with malware that enabled the hackers to manipulate data on targeted systems, “resulting in operational disruption and financial loss,” according to the advisory.
The notice, which was published amid ongoing hostilities between the US, Iran, and Israel, expands the number of impacted systems from just the Rockwell Automation PLC systems that Iran exploited earlier this year to also include Schneider Electric, Siemens, and that “potentially all internet exposed PLCs” may be impacted. Critical infrastructure operators are instructed to take action to protect their systems as, according to the advisory, the Iran-linked hackers are “conducting this activity to cause disruptive effects within the United States.”

title: Best Laptops (2026): My Top Recommendations After Testing Hundreds
summary: I’ve been reviewing laptops for over a decade, and here's my advice on how to find the right laptop for you.
full_text:
I’ve been reviewing laptops for well over a decade, sometimes testing more than 30 devices per year. They aren’t all winners, and many should be avoided, no matter how slick the marketing or cheap the discount. Good news: It’s my job to recommend laptops that fit your budget and won’t make you regret your purchase six months later. These are my favorite laptops that I’ve tested myself and would highly recommend you buy.
For more guidance, also see my recommendations in specific categories, such as the Best MacBooks, Best Gaming Laptops, Best Chromebooks, Best Budget Laptops, Best Windows Laptops, and Best 2-in-1 Laptops. My guide on How to Choose a Laptop may also help if you’re undecided.
Updated July 2026: I’ve reevaluated the laptop landscape given recent price increases, including Apple’s MacBook lineup. I’ve also included notes from my recent testing of the Dell 14S.
The Laptops I Recommend Most
When friends or family ask what laptop to buy, I always start with the MacBook Air. It is far more powerful than its compact size suggests. It’s a shame about the recent $200 price increase from $1,099 to $1,299, but even at that new price, it remains my top pick because it nails the big picture. Everything from the trackpad to the speakers are of the highest quality, and it delivers all the performance and battery life the average person needs.
With the latest M5 chip, its GPU matches the M3 Pro MacBook Pro, easily handling everything from gaming to video editing. That’s not at all what the MacBook Air is designed for, but the performance is there when you want to dabble. It’s what makes it feel like a do-it-all machine, all contained in a fanless chassis that’s still one of the thinnest laptops you can buy. Oh, and did I mention it’ll last well over a full work day away from the wall socket and perform just as well on battery as when plugged in? In almost every aspect, it’s the gold standard.
While the lower price of the new MacBook Neo might be tempting, the MacBook Air is the better choice for anyone working at a computer all day. With its superior performance, extra memory, faster storage, and Thunderbolt ports, you will never have to question if you have the right tool for the job. (And unless you already know you need a MacBook Pro, you probably don’t.)
If you prefer Windows or need it for specific applications, the HP OmniBook Ultra 14 is the strongest alternative to the MacBook Air. It might just be the best laptop HP has ever made. The device is beautifully built and incredibly sturdy, with a thin chassis (though the height of the feet makes it taller on the table next to the MacBook Air), an oversized haptic trackpad, and polished metal edges. I also appreciate the three Thunderbolt 4 ports split between both sides for convenient charging, as well as the surprisingly good speakers.
I tested the high-end model, which features a fast Snapdragon X2 Elite, 32 GB of RAM, and a gorgeous 2880 x 1800 OLED display. The screen offers near-perfect colors, excellent brightness, and astounding HDR performance. It doesn’t get much better than this. My only real complaint is that the glossy OLED screen is quite reflective and lacks an anti-glare coating. It’s hoped there will soon be more configuration options, as I’d love to see this higher-end OLED panel available in a cheaper configuration. (The base configuration sold directly from HP has a dimmer, lower resolution screen.)
My other favorite alternative to the 15-inch MacBook Air is the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x. I was impressed by the overall package for this laptop. The price has increased since I reviewed it, up from $900 to $1,150. But compared with the competition, it still rises to the top, primarily thanks to its fantastic 2560 x 1600 OLED display with a 165-Hz refresh rate. I highly recommend spending the $30 to upgrade from the base screen (sold on Amazon) to this excellent OLED version (sold by Lenovo). Additionally, while it is slightly thicker than the MacBook Air, that extra space allows for a great selection of ports, including HDMI, USB-A, and an SD card slot. The Snapdragon X2 Plus isn’t quite an M5 killer, but I was happy with the performance and battery life provided. While I can no longer say it’s the best laptop under $1,000, in a world where laptop pricing keeps increasing, it’s the best value for what you get.
If you are actually shopping for a laptop under $1,000, I’d point you in the direction of the Dell 14 Plus. It came out last year, and in recent months it’s become one of the few Windows laptops worth buying at this price. It has a sharp screen, a decent touchpad, and great battery life. Performance is solid too, using previous-gen Intel chips and 16 GB of RAM. The Dell 14 Plus is exactly that, and it’s currently the best Windows laptop you can buy for less than $1,000.
I used to recommend the Surface Laptop 13.8 (also known as the 7th Edition) as one of my top picks. While I still love this laptop, it’s risen in price dramatically and no longer feels like as good of a value, especially since it’s two years old. The 2024 model now starts at $1,200, while the next-generation model with the Snapdragon X2 chips costs $1,700.
Cheap Laptops That Are Actually Good
While “cheap” means something different to everyone, the best budget laptops generally fall under $750. This is where Windows truly shines, offering great specs for less money. Thanks to the latest processors from Qualcomm and Intel, these laptops now offer battery life that rivals Apple. The best affordable laptop I’ve checked out is the HP OmniBook 5. The model I tested has a Snapdragon X processor, 16 GB of RAM, 512 GB of storage, and a 14-inch OLED screen. Discounts fluctuate frequently, but right now you can buy the 256-GB model directly from HP for $630. That’s a killer deal.
I also recently tested the new HP OmniBook 3, which uses the same chip as the OmniBook 5. It frequently sells for less than the OmniBook 5 by at least a $100 or so. While the OmniBook 3 is a good alternative, the OmniBook 5 is much thinner and looks more modern. Neither laptop has a particularly great touchpad, which is easily the biggest flaw in both laptops. The OmniBook 5 is the better buy if you can afford it, though.
The MacBook Neo is Apple’s new entry-level laptop. It initially started at an aggressive $599, but that price has recently been raised to $699. Even at that price, the laptop shines when it comes to the display. It offers the best screen you can find at this price, bringing the macOS experience to an unprecedented value, even at $699 (or $799 for the 512 GB model). Apple clearly gave priority to the front-of-screen experience, delivering a premium feel across the display, build quality, and keyboard. While the 8 GB of RAM, outdated ports, and slower SSD are notable drawbacks—making the MacBook Air a better choice for remote workers—the Neo is the most premium-feeling laptop available for students, travelers, and casual users.
Given how good some of these budget laptops are, it’s a bit harder to find a place for Chromebooks. The standout option is still the Lenovo Chromebook Plus 14. It’s the most premium Chromebook available, with an OLED screen, 16 GB of RAM, and battery life that rivals the MacBook Neo. Its price just keep going up, though, now up to $849. That’s far too expensive for what you get.
Instead, I recommend the Acer Chromebook Plus 516, which is the best of the cheaper Chromebooks. While it’s a bit thick and the screen isn’t the sharpest (especially for a 16-inch laptop), it’s the best laptop you can buy for under $500, and it occasionally dips down to $349. Acer didn’t skimp on the quality of the touchpad, either, which I appreciate. Windows laptops are about to get much stronger in this category, however, just as higher-priced Chromebooks will be seemingly phased out over time and replaced by the upcoming Googlebooks.

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Was Made for Imax 70mm. Good Luck Watching It That Way
summary: Over the last several years, the Imax format has taken on a few different forms—but only a few dozen theaters are capable of screening it in its full glory.
full_text:
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey in Imax 70mm is the hottest club in town, if you can get in.
While Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s epic is available on thousands of screens around the world, there are only 41—including 25 in the US—that can offer it in full Imax 70mm glory. Many of those are sold out for weeks. Levels of FOMO are off the charts.
That’s partly because The Odyssey is the first feature film shot entirely on Imax film with Imax cameras. For the uninitiated, the Imax film format takes an already large 65-mm film negative and runs it through the camera horizontally, resulting in an image 15 perforations wide compared to the standard 5 perf. When projected on a giant Imax screen, the resulting image, with a squarish aspect ratio of 1.43:1, is enormous and incredibly sharp, creating a far more immersive experience than standard cinema offerings. This is real Imax, according to fans of the format, which was first introduced in 1970.
Imax, though, comes in a variety of flavors: digital formats in 2K and 4K resolutions, xenon and laser light configurations, on top of the classic 15/70-mm. Outside of a select few, most digital Imax theaters crop the image to a wider 1.90:1 aspect ratio and project on screens a good deal smaller than a traditional Imax giant theater.
“This all started in 2008 when Imax introduced its first digital system,” says James Hyder, who managed the Smithsonian Air and Space Museum’s Langley Imax theater in the ’80s, and ran the giant-screen industry journal LF Examiner from 2008 to 2021. Imax did not respond to requests for comment.
The company’s foray into digital exhibition with a 2K-resolution dual-projector system was part of a long-planned shift. Executives wanted to expand beyond museums and science centers and into big theater chains, which didn’t always have the screen real estate the traditional Imax experience demands.
The result, though, has been notably different Imax experiences depending on what type of Imax theater you’re in. Especially as major theater chains have invested in PLF (Premium Large Format) screens that rely on Dolby Vision or other systems, it’s hard to know what you’re going to get, or if Imax is even your best bet.
Complicating things further for The Odyssey is that it’s available in so many premium formats—six, altogether—that the film’s official website includes a guide to their various strengths and aspect ratios. While it disambiguates between 70mm Imax and “regular” Imax, it doesn’t capture the wide range of what those “regular” experiences can entail.
“It's a disservice to their customers, and it's basically trading on a reputation for real giant screens that used to be what Imax stood for,” Hyder says of the lack of clarity and consistency around how Imax is implemented.
Recent years have seen a resurgence in shooting and projecting on film, with Imax 70mm in particular becoming the gold standard. Nolan’s films regularly get Imax 70mm releases on the few screens that can accommodate it, but following the success of Oppenheimer, a string of releases, including Dune: Part Two, Sinners, One Battle After Another, and Project Hail Mary, have followed suit.
While The Odyssey was shot in a 1.43:1 aspect ratio, its images were composed to function just as well when cropped to other ratios, all the way down to the very wide 2.39:1. It was intentionally shot to work across digital, 35-mm, and regular 5-perf/70-mm, all overseen by the director and reflective of his intent. Eventually, it will also be available to buy on Blu-ray or stream online. It’s not unlike the difference between seeing a print or digital image of the Mona Lisa—which most people will in their lifetimes—and actually being lucky enough to see it in person at the Louvre.
Of course, there’s only one Mona Lisa, while there are a few dozen places to see The Odyssey on Imax 70mm. Still, the relative scarcity understandably leaves many wanting more. They may not get it any time soon.
“The problem is they haven’t made new Imax film projectors in about 50 years,” Imax CEO Rich Gelfond told Variety in a recent interview. “So we retrofit them, rebuild them, and part of our strategy is to see how far we can take it. But certainly, demand-driven, I’d like to see more.” Variety also reported that sources at the company say many of the specialized parts needed to build a new Imax film projector “simply no longer exist.”
In truth, Imax was still building new projectors in the late ’90s and early ’00s, and engineers can surely always find ways of machining new parts. But even Hyder agrees the difficulties and costs involved would make such an endeavor unlikely, and even unnecessary given the advances of digital projection. “It's the old chicken-and-egg problem. If you don't have a projector, if you don't have a theater to show it, you can't make the film. If you don't have the film to show in the theater, you can't show it in the theater,” Hyder says.
A 4K laser alternative to the full 1.43:1 experience of Imax 70mm does exist on some old giant Imax screens, and while it has its own advantages, it lacks the sharpness of the film format. To really get to an acceptable digital replacement for the 15/70-mm experience, Hyder speculates 8K projection would be needed, which could be done by tiling multiple 4K projectors across a single screen. “In fact, that’s what planetariums do all the time,” he says, noting that Imax itself has been supplanted by competitors on formerly Imax-branded giant dome screens.
Of course, there are other reasons Imax and exhibitors might not mind the scarcity of theaters that can screen the 15/70-mm format. “One of the reasons this is so popular is because it's rare,” Hyder says.
That said, Hyder is still happy to see so much attention on Imax 70mm, especially since he didn’t expect the format to still be alive in 2026. With good maintenance, the hefty machines could still run for decades more. “The last Imax film projector may still be running in 50 years with prints that are 20 or 50 years old,” he says. “The excitement [Imax film] creates still may not be enough to justify expanding it from the point of view of the financial people, but at least it’s still here.” It just might take a few weeks to snag a ticket.

title: GoPro Mission 1 Pro Review: The Best Action Camera You Can Buy
summary: GoPro’s New Mission 1 cameras bring action cameras to a higher level with a larger sensor and more cinematic footage.
full_text:
GoPro shook up the action camera world earlier this year, announcing the Mission 1 series of cameras, offering 8K video and the biggest image sensor you can get in an action camera. The Mission 1 series is now here, and after spending several months shooting with it on bikes, paddleboards, sailboats, zip lines, and more, I can say with confidence that this is the best action camera you can buy.
The Mission 1 Pro offers sharp, clear 8K footage with class-leading color-accurate video, excellent dynamic range, and great low-light performance (a place where other GoPro's have struggled). And they're every bit as waterproof, durable, and capable as you'd expect from a GoPro. The downside is that the $699 price also makes this the most expensive action camera you can buy, meaning it's not necessarily the GoPro for everyone.
A Pro-Level GoPro
Anyone who has ever tuned in for a GoPro earnings call (could be just me) knows that GoPro has long wanted to make a camera aimed at cinema professionals. That's what the Mission 1 series is—it's the Hero camera but with video quality that can be mixed with cinema-level cameras. There are three Mission 1 cameras, the entry level Mission 1, the slightly better Mission 1 Pro, and the Mission 1 Pro ILS, which uses interchangeable lenses based on the Micro Four Thirds mount. The ILS is the model that pro filmmakers will probably be most drawn to, while the other two cameras, while still chock-full of features for pros, will appeal to the original GoPro audience—those of us looking for a tough camera that can withstand just about any adventure.
The ILS model hasn't been released, but both the Mission 1 and Mission 1 Pro are available today. I've been testing the latter for several months. The differences between the Pro and non-Pro models are minimal, mostly in terms of frame rates that are available to each. Generally speaking the Pro can shoot higher frame rates and is better for slow-motion footage.

title: Contagious Cancer Found in North American Catfish
summary: Scientists identified the first known cancer transmissible among freshwater fish in a lake that spans the US and Canada.
full_text:
The idea that cancer could behave like a contagious disease may seem absurd; in humans, cancer cannot be transmitted from one person to another. Yet nature is still full of surprises. In exceptional cases, cancer cells themselves can pass from one individual to another and continue to multiply in a new host. This rare phenomenon has been detected in animals such as dogs, Tasmanian devils, and some species of mollusks, and it seems we can add one more to that exclusive club: catfish.
An international team of researchers has identified a transmissible melanoma in the brown catfish (Ameiurus nebulosus)—the first documented case in fish and also the first recorded in a freshwater ecosystem. Their findings were reported this month in the journal Nature.
An Impossible Pattern
The story began in 2012, when fishermen and biologists detected an unusually high number of catfish with black lesions in Lake Memphremagog, a body of water straddling Vermont and Quebec. Previous studies revealed that these spots were malignant melanomas, and that between 23 percent and 37 percent of the specimens examined had these tumors—an unusually high incidence for this species.
“That was surprising,” said Julie Dragon, a researcher at the University of Vermont and co-lead author of the study. “We wanted to know how a bottom-dwelling fish was getting a cancer we associate with exposure to too much sunlight.”
Initially, it was thought that the cause might be some toxic substance or a pathogen linked to pollution. One suspicion was that the flooding caused by Tropical Storm Irene in 2011 had degraded water quality by washing environmental pollutants into the lake. There were also concerns about the health of the lake, which supplies drinking water to more than 175,000 people. However, initial genetic analyses began to point in an unexpected direction.
It was then that the researchers wondered whether the tumors were descended from a single original cancer that had learned to spread among individual fish, rather than arising independently in each fish.
To test this unusual hypothesis, the team sequenced the complete genomes of tumors and healthy tissues from affected fish, and compared the data with that from healthy specimens from different populations.
The results indicated that the tumor cells from different fish were much more closely related to one another than to the animals in which they developed. In other words, the tumors shared their own genetic identity, distinct from that of their hosts. Furthermore, hundreds of thousands of genetic variants appeared repeatedly in the tumors but were absent from the healthy tissues of the same fish.
Such a pattern would be virtually impossible if each melanoma had arisen independently. By way of comparison, the researchers analyzed hundreds of human melanomas and found that nearly all of their mutations were unique to each patient. In contrast, most of the mutations present in the tumors of these fish were shared by numerous individuals—a hallmark of a transmissible clonal cancer.
Another possibility was that a virus or some microorganism was causing the melanomas. But after examining the genetic material in the samples, no viruses or bacteria specifically associated with the tumors were found. Although they cannot rule out the possibility that a pathogen may have played a role in the cancer’s origin or facilitated its spread, the evidence suggests that the transmissible agent is the cancer cells themselves.
Unanswered Questions
It is still unclear how this cancer is transmitted among catfish. The authors propose several possibilities. During reproduction, catfish congregate in confined spaces and maintain close physical contact, which could ease the exchange of cells. It is also possible that tumor cells survive temporarily in the water or in sediments and enter other fish through the skin, gills, or mouth. Another hypothesis is that hormonal changes associated with reproduction alter the immune response and promote the establishment of cancer.
“It seems to only happen in larger fish that are of spawning age,” said biologist Mark Henderson, a co-author of the study, regarding the absence of cancer in younger fish. “Maybe some part of spawning behavior leads to the spreading of the cancer between animals.”
In a release from the University of Vermont, the researchers noted that the tumor cells contained elevated levels of arsenic and that they observed a correlation between the geographic distribution of the cancer and areas with high natural concentrations of this element. They emphasize, however, that this association does not prove that arsenic is the cause of the cancer.
Despite the concerns, the scientists also note that the phenomenon could open up new avenues of research into cancer development, including in humans. “By studying how cancers survive and spread outside their original host, we can learn a great deal about what keeps cancers contained—and what happens when those boundaries break down,” said Dragon. Meanwhile, Henderson had advice for anglers.
“Personally,” he said, “I wouldn’t eat the ones with tumors.”
This story originally appeared on WIRED en Español and has been translated from Spanish.

title: How Many Electrolytes Should You Be Taking, and Can You Have Too Many?
summary: Electrolyte powders promise better hydration, energy, and recovery. But unless you’re losing serious fluid, water and food probably have you covered.
full_text:
Electrolyte powders, dissolvable tablets, and trendy ready-to-drink waters have graduated from the pockets of athletes to one of wellness’s buzziest categories.
And it’s a crowded market, worth an estimated $39 billion globally in 2025 and forecast to double within the next decade. Much of the growth has been fueled by wellness trends and influencer-fronted hype cycles, like Prime Hydration, created by YouTubers Logan Paul and KSI, which the company claimed pushed past $1 billion in sales in a single year. In other internet corners, dozens of celebrity and podcaster-adjacent brands are all promising a means of optimizing your way to hydration.
These products are marketed as daily essentials for everyone—from office workers to gym regulars—promising to combat brain fog, improve skin, banish fatigue, and aid recovery. Here’s everything you need to know about the electrolyte obsession, and when these products are actually worth buying.
What Are Electrolytes?
Electrolytes are essential minerals, among them sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, and chloride, that carry an electrical charge once dissolved in fluid. That charge is what lets the body do much of its basic work, such as helping muscles and nerves work correctly. They work to ensure fluid stays balanced inside and outside every cell, as a serious imbalance can cause headaches, muscle cramps, dizziness, fatigue, and weakness. In more serious cases, severe electrolyte imbalances can interfere with heart function and require medical treatment.
Who Needs Electrolytes?
For most healthy adults, the body has been regulating electrolyte levels perfectly well long before trendy, flavored hydration sticks landed on supermarket shelves. In fact, if you eat a reasonably balanced diet and drink water when you’re thirsty, there’s a good chance you’re already getting everything you need.
The sachet earns its place in roughly three situations. Studies from the American College of Sports Medicine suggest that water alone is sufficient for exercise lasting less than an hour, but electrolytes become increasingly useful during longer sessions of prolonged, sweat-heavy exercise, particularly in high temperatures or humidity. They're also useful for illness involving heavy fluid loss, which is why oral rehydration salts are a recognized medical treatment rather than a wellness trend. And you should also consider them during long stretches of fasting, when the food that usually supplies these minerals is absent.
Are There Natural Electrolytes?
There are many sources of electrolytes in everyday foods. If you’re eating a reasonably varied diet (fruits, vegetables, lean protein, whole grains, nuts, seeds), your electrolyte stores are continually being topped up without the need for specialist drinks or powders.
Research by the Beverage Hydration Index shows that milk-based drinks can maintain hydration for longer than plain water. The combination of protein, natural electrolytes and small amounts of fat slows the rate at which fluid leaves the stomach, helping the body retain hydration for longer. Coconut water too can replenish potassium.
The Nutrition Source from Harvard’s School of Public Health notes that, essentially, “any beverage containing electrolyte minerals may be labeled an electrolyte drink. Some are very costly yet only contain a small amount of these nutrients, while others may contain a high amount of only one nutrient such as potassium or sodium.”
Can You Have Too Many Electrolytes?
For healthy adults, an occasional electrolyte drink is unlikely to cause harm. Daily consumption, however, can sometimes be counterproductive.
Many electrolyte products contain significant amounts of sodium, despite the fact that most populations already consume considerably more salt than recommended. The World Health Organization estimates the global average of sodium intake a day is more than double its recommended limit and roughly 1.89 million deaths a year can be linked to excess intake. Regularly adding extra sodium may not be ideal for anyone managing high blood pressure or cardiovascular risk. Some formulations also contain substantial amounts of added sugar, making them nutritionally closer to soft drinks than health products.
Anyone recovering from illness or sweating through an August shift outdoors has a fair case for supplementing. For everyone else, the best approach to hydration remains an unremarkable one. Electrolytes themselves are nonnegotiable. Electrolyte products are mostly just a lifestyle purchase.
This story originally appeared on WIRED Middle East.

title: Sony 收掉 aibo 機器狗，深圳賣出 13,361 台成人陪伴機器人
summary:
優必選 6 月 30 日在深圳發表消費級人形機器人 UWORLD U1 系列，U1 Ultra 男版售價 99 […]

〈Sony 收掉 aibo 機器狗，深圳賣出 13,361 台成人陪伴機器人〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
優必選 6 月 30 日在深圳發表消費級人形機器人 UWORLD U1 系列，U1 Ultra 男版售價 99 萬人民幣、女版 88 萬人民幣，官方宣稱線上線下通路預購累計突破 13,361 台。這款機器人明確不做家事、僅售成年使用者，唯一功能是陪伴。而在此五天前，Sony 才剛公告機器狗 aibo 在日本國內停售。
（前情提要：中國少子化怪 AI 頭上，數百萬人被迫跟 AI 伴侶「分手」）
（背景補充：中國人形機器人以 80% 市佔率搶先全球，但真正能獲利目前只有這兩領域）
重點摘要
- 優必選 UWORLD U1 系列 6/30 發表，U1 Lite 11.98 萬人民幣、U1 Pro 16.98 萬、U1 Ultra 男版 99 萬
- 官方稱全通路預購 13,361 台，但 7/8 京東平台顯示預售僅 5,613 件，3,000 元訂金可無理由全退
- 優必選 2025 年全尺寸人形機器人只賣出 1,079 台，年化產能逾 6,000 台、利用率不到兩成
六月三十日，深圳。一名日本科技記者站在優必選 2026 全球發布會現場，看著台上那個穿著整齊、頭髮吹過、脖子會微微轉動的身影，寫下自己的第一反應：一瞬間，我以為那是人。
日本科技圈當天吵的不是規格，是恐怖谷。心理學家森政弘 1970 年畫的那條曲線說，機器越像人越討喜，直到某個臨界點，好感突然翻轉成毛骨悚然。半個世紀以來，沒人敢把量產品押在那道懸崖邊。
而過去兩年，人形機器人的戰場一直在工廠。搬箱子、分揀、質檢，比誰更能替代一個人力。特斯拉的 Optimus、Figure、現代汽車的 Atlas，打的全是同一場仗。
但優必選這次賣的東西，產品說明上明確寫著不做家事。
不掃地，不煮飯，不洗碗。僅面向成年使用者，唯一功能是陪你。
Sony 關掉 aibo 的第五天
六月二十五日，Sony 官網掛出公告：機器狗 aibo ERS-1000 在日本國內庫存售完即停售，修理與訂閱服務照舊。
aibo 是機器狗賽道的開拓者。1999 年 5 月首批三千台在網路上二十分鐘售罄，單價超過 2000 美元。但 7 年下來只賣出約 15 萬台，大約是 Sony 商業計畫預估的十分之一，2006 年 1 月整個消費機器人部門連同 aibo 一起被砍。2018 年復活過一次，2026 年再次收攤。
99 萬和 88 萬的差別
UWORLD U1 分三個型號：上半身的 U1 Lite 定價 11.98 萬人民幣，全身的 U1 Pro 16.98 萬，旗艦 U1 Ultra 男版 99 萬、女版 88 萬。男版身高 183 公分、42 公斤，女版 168 公分、35.2 公斤。
男版比女版貴 11 萬人民幣。差別是身高差 15 公分，體重多了 6.8 公斤。
官方規格寫得很滿，88 個自由度、覆蓋人類 90% 基礎動作、可辨識二十多種情緒且準確率逾九成。矽膠皮膚做出了毛孔、血管與指紋紋理，還能用 3D 臉部重建加聲音複製，還原特定一個人的長相與聲音。
日媒把 U1 Ultra 男版直接換算成 2,376 萬日圓，然後加了四個字：成人限定。
首批秒殺
6 月 2 日在京東開賣，八天突破三千台；6 月 30 日發布會當天，執行長周劍宣布全通路累計突破 13,361 台。這個數字是廠商自行公布，不是第三方查核結果。
aibo 的三千台，二十分鐘賣完。軟銀的 Pepper 更誇張，2015 年 6 月消費版開賣，首批一千台六十秒售罄。五年後軟銀停產，總產量約兩萬七千台。
眉毛是手工植的
2025 年優必選全尺寸人形機器人全年賣出 1,079 台，收入 8.21 億人民幣；同年總營收 20.01 億、虧損 7.9 億。而 2024 年的同類出貨量，是 3 台。
截至 2025 年底，這條產線年化產能逾 6,000 台，利用率不到兩成。宣布的預購量已是年產能的兩倍多。而仿生機器人單台頭部有兩三千個零部件，眉毛、睫毛與皮膚紋理仰賴人工，沒有全自動化產線。
到 7 月 8 日，京東平台顯示的預售數量是 5,613 件，發布會後新增不到 200 台。而 3,000 元訂金可無理由全額退回，退單沒有任何違約成本。
市場已經給過答案。發布當日優必選股價盤中一度漲 18%，7 月 3 日再漲近 18%；質疑聲湧上來後，7 月 6 日單日重挫 10.01%。
460 億人民幣砸下去，先落地的是孤獨
這不是一家公司的豪賭，是整條賽道的水位。2026 年上半年，中國具身智慧與機器人領域發生 288 起融資，揭露金額超過 460 億人民幣，其中前二十家就拿走約 330 億。
錢多到這種程度，最先被量產出來的落地場景不是工廠，是客廳。
優必選鎖定的客群很直接：都市單身族群，以及動漫與乙女遊戲的愛好者。日媒引述中國報導，實際想定的購買層是三十五到五十歲的都市單身中產。這門生意叫「情緒消費」。
而就在七月，中國才剛以少子化為由把一批 AI 伴侶 App 下架，數百萬人被迫跟自己的虛擬伴侶分手。
軟體的陪伴被關掉，硬體的陪伴正在出貨。
倫理質疑當然來了，機器人會造成情感依賴、等同一台會走路的監視攝影機。優必選的回應是成立倫理委員會、資料本地處理、限成年人購買。
常見問題
UWORLD U1 人形機器人多少錢？能做家事嗎？
U1 Lite 售價 11.98 萬人民幣、U1 Pro 16.98 萬，旗艦 U1 Ultra 男版 99 萬、女版 88 萬。官方明確表示不承擔清潔、烹飪等家務，定位是家庭情感陪伴，且僅面向成年使用者銷售。
13,361 台預購訂單可信嗎？
這是優必選官方公布的全通路累計數字，未經第三方查核。7 月 8 日京東平台顯示預售 5,613 件，且 3,000 元訂金可無理由全退，實際成交量要等 9 月 16 日起交付才驗得出來。

title: Robinhood 洽談 Crypto.com 供應事件交易，Kalshi 最大通路成對手
summary:
《華爾街日報》報導，Robinhood 正與 Crypto.com 洽談合作，計畫讓用戶直接在 Robinho […]

〈Robinhood 洽談 Crypto.com 供應事件交易，Kalshi 最大通路成對手〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
《華爾街日報》報導，Robinhood 正與 Crypto.com 洽談合作，計畫讓用戶直接在 Robinhood 的預測市場專區交易 Crypto.com 的「是／否」合約，知情人士說談判仍在進行、不保證成局。Robinhood 原本主要靠 Kalshi 供貨，但它今年 1 月完成收購、夏天開張的自家交易所 Rothera 把費率壓到 Kalshi 的一半，雙方關係正從合作轉向競爭。
（前情提要：嘉信理財聯手 Cboe 推出標普 500「事件型選擇權」，華爾街巨頭入局預測市場）
（背景補充：預測市場怎麼玩？四大平台實測，訂單簿與自動做市各有眉角）
預測市場的供貨戰，打到了 Robinhood 的交易介面上。《華爾街日報》報導，Robinhood 正與 Crypto.com 洽談合作，讓用戶直接在 Robinhood 現有的預測市場專區，交易 Crypto.com 提供的「是／否」合約。知情人士說，談判還在進行，不保證會成局。
重點不在多一個合作夥伴，而在 Robinhood 的供貨名單越拉越長，長到原本的主力供應商開始緊張。
Kalshi 從夥伴變對手
Robinhood 去年開始上架 Kalshi 的事件合約，用戶可以對體育賽事結果、聯準會利率決策這類事件下注。除了 Kalshi，它的供貨方還有 Interactive Brokers 旗下的 ForecastEx。
問題是 Robinhood 自己也下場了。它與 Susquehanna International Group 合資的交易所 Rothera，今年 1 月完成對 CFTC 持牌交易所 MIAXdx 的收購，今年夏天開始營運，Robinhood 隨後就把一部分事件合約導進自家平台。
費率是最直接的訊號。Rothera 每口合約收費上限 1 美分，跟 ForecastEx 差不多，只有 Kalshi 上限 2 美分的一半。分析師已經觀察到，Kalshi 的交易量裡來自 Robinhood 客戶的比重正在下滑。
Crypto.com 帶進來的不只是合約
Crypto.com 在這條賽道推得很兇。2024 年底先透過衍生品業務提供事件合約，今年 2 月推出獨立的預測市場平台 OG。
更值得看的是它的通路布局。去年 10 月底，川普媒體科技集團宣布與 Crypto.com 旗下的 CDNA 獨家合作，在 Truth Social 上推出預測市場產品 Truth Predict，涵蓋政治選舉、利率與通膨、黃金原油價格到體育賽事。社群平台直接內建預測市場，這是第一家。
換句話說，Robinhood 談的不是一個單純的合約供應商，而是一個已經自己開好通路的同業。
這條賽道現在有多大
規模已經不是小數目。動區先前報導，Kalshi 在世界盃期間吃下 543 億美元交易量，是 Polymarket 的 2.6 倍，光這一屆就替它帶進約 300 萬新用戶。對照之下，今年超級碗相關市場的交易量約 9 億美元，差了兩個量級。
Robinhood 這邊，2025 年全年交易的事件合約超過 120 億口，2026 年到目前為止已經超過 160 億口，是它成長最快的產品線之一。
所以這場談判真正在談的，是 Robinhood 要不要再找一個人來填自己的貨架。對 Kalshi 來說，麻煩的地方在於這個貨架本來有很大一塊是它的。

title: 川普空軍一號有被刺殺危險！紐時揭伊朗密謀發射飛彈
summary:
《紐約時報》引述多名知情人士報導，美國總統川普本月出席土耳其安卡拉北約峰會期間，美方偵測到伊朗與其代理勢力可能 […]

〈川普空軍一號有被刺殺危險！紐時揭伊朗密謀發射飛彈〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
《紐約時報》引述多名知情人士報導，美國總統川普本月出席土耳其安卡拉北約峰會期間，美方偵測到伊朗與其代理勢力可能朝總統專機發射飛彈，特勤局因此建議他離開安卡拉時改搭舊版空軍一號。卡達捐贈的這架 4 億美元波音 747-8 尚未裝上與舊機同級的防禦系統。川普原先說換機只是要讓駐英美軍參觀新機，與安全無關。
（前情提要：川普警告伊朗：若胡塞武裝再犯，將面臨「重大軍事懲罰」！）
（背景補充：美對伊朗連13晚空襲、布蘭特原油破百，比特幣被逼退6.4萬美元）
重點摘要
- 紐時揭伊朗代理勢力謀劃朝川普專機射飛彈，特勤局建議他離開安卡拉時換機
- 卡達捐贈的 4 億美元波音 747-8 尚未裝上舊空軍一號等級的反飛彈防禦系統
- 白宮稱新專機「完全安全」，但今年秋季仍要進廠升級約一個月
川普說，他在土耳其換飛機是為了讓駐英美軍參觀新的空軍一號，跟安全一點關係都沒有。《紐約時報》的版本不太一樣。多名知情人士向該報透露，美方當時偵測到伊朗與其盟友代理勢力策劃朝總統專機發射飛彈的可信圖謀，特勤局因此建議川普離開安卡拉前換機。
事情發生在本月 7 日至 8 日的北約安卡拉峰會。川普飛抵土耳其時搭的是卡達捐贈的波音 747-8，這架造價約 4 億美元的新專機去年才交到美方手上，改裝了好幾個月才正式接手總統的行程。峰會結束後，他改搭舊版空軍一號從安卡拉飛往英國，等到要飛回美國的最後一段，才又換回新機。
知情人士強調，這個威脅的目標不是那架卡達飛機本身，而是川普這個人，以及任何一架載著他的飛機。換句話說，換機不是為了躲開針對某架飛機的攻擊，是為了換上一架真的擋得住攻擊的飛機。
舊飛機有雷射，新飛機還沒有
兩架飛機的差別在防禦系統。服役多年的舊版空軍一號配有能致盲來襲飛彈的雷射裝置，以及讓彈藥偏離目標的誘導系統，這些是幾十年來針對總統專機威脅一層層堆出來的配備。卡達捐的這架 747-8 目前裝了哪些防禦裝置，外界並不清楚，可以確定的是還沒到舊機的水準。
這架飛機從一開始就爭議不斷。2025 年卡達提出致贈時，美國國內就吵過收下外國政府 4 億美元禮物是否妥當，卡達總理當時的回應是這在盟友之間很正常。
白宮說完全安全，秋天還要再改一個月
白宮的回應是這架飛機沒問題。發言人 Karoline Leavitt 表示，新的空軍一號「對總統的出行完全安全，但秋季將獲得額外的升級與強化」。川普自己則說，接下來一個月飛機的能力會被「拉滿」。
一架完全安全的飛機，為什麼還需要再進廠改一個月，這兩句話要同時成立，難度不低。比較合理的讀法是，新機的機艙與外觀早就準備好了，真正費工的軍規防禦系統還在後面排隊。
這件事的時間點也不輕鬆。美方在此之前就已經收到伊朗方面可能策劃針對川普行動的情報，對總統的安全威脅等級一直維持在高檔。動區稍早報導過，美軍對伊朗的空襲已經連續進行十三個晚上，布蘭特原油一度衝破每桶 100 美元，川普本人也在 7 月 23 日公開警告伊朗，胡塞武裝若再動手將面臨「重大軍事懲罰」。他警告的正是這次被點名的代理勢力。
真正要盯的是秋天那次進廠。在伊朗與代理勢力的威脅沒有降溫之前，那架 4 億美元的專機能不能在下一趟出訪前把防禦補齊，比它的內裝值多少錢重要得多。
常見問題
川普為什麼在土耳其臨時換飛機？
紐約時報引述知情人士指出，美方偵測到伊朗與其代理勢力策劃朝總統專機發射飛彈的可信圖謀，特勤局因此建議川普離開安卡拉時改搭舊版空軍一號。川普本人先前的說法是換機為了讓駐英美軍參觀新機。
卡達捐贈的空軍一號缺少什麼防禦能力？
舊版空軍一號配有可致盲來襲飛彈的雷射裝置與誘導偏移系統，卡達捐贈的這架 4 億美元波音 747-8 尚未達到同級水準。白宮表示該機今年秋季將再進行約一個月的升級與強化。
本文參考《紐約時報》與 CBS News 報導，由動區動趨整理報導。

title: ChatGPT、Codex 錯誤率飆高！OpenAI 22 項服務同時降級，5天內8次大型事故
summary:
OpenAI 官方狀態頁在臺灣時間 7 月 25 日下午 5 點 17 分掛出新事故，標題是 Elevated […]

〈ChatGPT、Codex 錯誤率飆高！OpenAI 22 項服務同時降級，5天內8次大型事故〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
OpenAI 官方狀態頁在臺灣時間 7 月 25 日下午 5 點 17 分掛出新事故，標題是 Elevated error rates（錯誤率升高），官方只留下一句「正在調查」，原因與恢復時間都沒有交代。被標成效能降級的元件有 22 項，除了 ChatGPT 與 Codex，連登入、對話、檔案、搜尋、Sora 與 VS Code 擴充套件都在名單上。這已經是 7 月 21 日以來的第八起事故。
（前情提要：OpenAI 承認自家 AI 模型意外駭進 Hugging Face）
（背景補充：Notion 一度中斷 Claude 模型連線，產品主管：只是暫時性服務故障）
重點摘要
- OpenAI 狀態頁 7/25 下午 5 點 17 分掛出「Elevated error rates」，狀態仍停在調查中
- 共 22 項服務被標為效能降級，整體列為 Partial System Degradation
- 翻事故列表，7 月 21 日至今官方已掛出八起事故，前七起皆已解決
OpenAI 官方狀態頁在台灣時間 7 月 25 日下午 5 點 17 分掛出一起新事故，標題寫的是 Elevated error rates，錯誤率升高。可以使用，但可能出錯的機率增加。
官方說明正在調查列表上這些服務的問題。沒有原因，沒有恢復時間。截至下午 5 點 50 分，事故狀態仍停在 investigating（調查中），已經超過半小時。
被列進清單的不只 ChatGPT 和 Codex。狀態頁上標成 degraded performance（效能降級）的元件一共 22 項，包含 Login、Conversations、Responses、Embeddings、Files、Search、Batch、Fine-tuning、Moderations、Sora、GPTs、Codex API、VS Code 擴充套件、ChatGPT Atlas 與 ChatGPT Work，整體狀態被標為 Partial System Degradation（部分系統降級）。
五天內第八起
官方把這次的影響分級標為 minor（輕微）。但把事故列表往回翻，畫面不太一樣。
- 7/21: 圖片生成在 ChatGPT 完全無法使用，分級 major
- 7/22: 檔案上傳與圖片生成錯誤，同日 Workspace Agent 錯誤
- 7/23: 一天掛三起，含 ChatGPT 錯誤率升高與 gpt-image-2 的 API 錯誤與延遲
- 7/24: Codex Review 錯誤升高
- 7/25: 本次事故
五天、八起，其中七起已標記解決，第八起還在調查。OpenAI 沒有說明這幾次之間有沒有關聯。
常見問題
ChatGPT 現在是不是掛了？
OpenAI 官方狀態頁 7 月 25 日臺灣時間下午 5 點 17 分起回報錯誤率升高，ChatGPT、Codex 等 22 項服務被標為效能降級，屬於部分降級而非完全停機，狀態頁截稿前仍顯示調查中。
這次故障影響哪些服務？
除了 ChatGPT 與 Codex，還包含 Login、Conversations、Responses、Embeddings、Files、Search、Batch、Fine-tuning、Sora、GPTs、Codex API、VS Code 擴充套件、ChatGPT Atlas 與 ChatGPT Work，開發者端與消費端同時受影響。

title: Unhappy Tottenham players should leave - De Zerbi
summary: Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto de Zerbi says players who are not "proud and happy to stay" at the club should leave.
full_text:
Unhappy Tottenham players should leave - De Zerbi
- Published
Tottenham manager Roberto de Zerbi says players who are not happy at the club this summer should move elsewhere.
The Italian, who took over at Spurs at the end of March and helped save them from Premier league relegation last season, made his comments amid doubts over Lucas Bergvall's future at the club.
Tottenham rejected a first bid of £38m from Nottingham Forest for Sweden midfielder Bergvall, with Forest set to up their offer to £45m.
"I was very clear at the start of my time in Tottenham. I said, who doesn't want to stay in Tottenham? Who is not happy, is not proud to stay here, has to leave," De Zerbi said, external before his side's pre-season friendly against Auckland FC in New Zealand on Sunday (04:30 BST).
"I want the players to be proud and happy to stay here, to go on the pitch in Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with big motivation. Because now in football, if you think also in the World Cup, the motivation makes the difference.
"The motivation is to be happy to stay in one team."
- Forest set to make £45m offer for Spurs' Bergvall - Published16 July
 
Tottenham not finished in transfer market
Bergvall, who joined Spurs from Swedish club Djurgarden in 2024, played limited minutes at the end of last season under De Zerbi.
The 20-year-old started the Italian's first game in charge – a 1-0 defeat at Sunderland – and, after that, made four appearances as a substitute.
Spurs have since signed midfielders Sandro Tonali - in a £100m deal from Newcastle United - and Mateus Fernandes for £85m from West Ham.
"I have not spoken with Lucas yet," said De Zerbi. "I will in the next days and we will make the best decision for the club, for Lucas, for me, for every one of us, without problems. Lucas is a big, big talent.
"There will be a big competition to play because at the end, I think we will be two players for each position.
"If he wants to stay, I will be happy. Otherwise, we have to find a new solution with [sporting director] Johan Lange, with [chief executive] Vinai [Venkatesham]. It's not my business after the decision to leave."
Tottenham have also added defenders Jan Paul van Hecke, Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi to their ranks and De Zerbi says now the "target is to complete the attacking positions".
"First of all, I think it's not finished yet, our transfer market window," he added. "We have to finish, we have to bring another couple of, maybe more, maybe not less, but a couple of players."
Bergvall is part of Tottenham's squad in New Zealand but wingers Mohammed Kudus (thigh) and Dejan Kulusevski (knee) have not travelled as they recover from long-term injuries.
"Kudus is very close. I think when we come back to London he will be available to start working with us," said De Zerbi. "It's a great thing for us. Kudus is another important player.
"Kulusevski, we have to see in the next couple of weeks. He's another important player. After one season, one complete season, without a game, we have to analyse better and better, don't take risks, first of all for him and then for us."
Meanwhile, Spurs attacking midfielder Xavi Simons said "the first four days were the worst days of my life" as he recalled the anterior cruciate ligament injury he suffered in April.
The Netherlands international required surgery on the serious knee injury and missed the 2026 World Cup.
"I couldn't sleep, I didn't eat for one week," he told Tottenham's website. "I was in a lot of pain. I was vomiting and felt dizzy, it was everything. That pain, I don't wish no-one to go through that pain.
"I don't know what it's like for other players but, for me, it was like my whole body was saying like 'what happened?'
"This is what it is. I'm happy and in a good place now."

title: 'Maybe he's a racist' - Trump critical of James
summary: United States President Donald Trump said LeBron James might be "a racist" when asked if the basketball star is the "best ever" to play the sport.
full_text:
'Maybe he's a racist' - Trump critical of James
- Published
United States President Donald Trump said LeBron James might be "a racist" when asked if the basketball star is the "best ever" to play the sport.
James, 41, announced on Friday he is set to continue his glittering career with the Philadelphia 76ers.
When asked about the move in a White House news conference later, Trump explained why he believed Michael Jordan was the better player.
Jordan, 63, won six NBA titles with the Chicago Bulls in the 1990s and NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP) five times.
When asked whether Jordan or James was the "best ever", Trump said: "Michael Jordan is a guy that's a friend of mine. I play golf with him. He's a really good guy.
"I think LeBron is, maybe he's a racist, but maybe he doesn't like Trump. I don't know. I only like people that like me, so I would say Michael Jordan all the way."
James, who has not responded to Trump's comment, has been a regular critic of Trump during his terms as president and endorsed Democrat candidates Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden and Kamala Harris when they ran against him.
In 2017 he referred to Trump as "a bum" following a row over invitations to the White House for NBA-winning teams.
James has won four NBA titles with the Miami Heat (twice), the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Los Angeles Lakers.
He has been named the league's MVP four times and is the NBA's all-time leader in points and games played.
James will be looking to secure a fifth title with the 76ers following his announcement on Friday that he is heading to Philadelphia.
They now boast the talents of James and All-Stars Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown.
"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team," James said in a lengthy post on social media.

title: Changes called for as Sinner and Djokovic withdraw from Canadian Open
summary: The tournament director of the Canadian Open says changes need to be made to the "demanding schedule" of players after Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic pull out of the Masters 1000 event.
full_text:
Changes called for as Sinner and Djokovic withdraw
- Published
The tournament director of the Canadian Open says changes need to be made to the "demanding schedule" of players after Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic pulled out of the Masters 1000 event.
Sinner, who beat Alexander Zverev to win the Wimbledon title this month, said he had withdrawn from the ATP tournament, which takes place from 2-13 August in Montreal, to prioritise his health.
Carlos Alcaraz will also be absent from the Canadian Open as he continues his recovery from a wrist injury that has kept him out since April.
"We are obviously very disappointed that Jannik and Novak won't be joining us in Montreal this year, especially after they also withdrew from last year's tournament in Toronto," said the Canadian Open's tournament director Valerie Tetreault.
"We respect their decisions and understand that, with such a demanding schedule, players' health must remain the priority.
"That said, we believe the frequency of these last-minute withdrawals in the last few years raises a broader issue for our sport.
"Masters 1000 events are among the flagship tournaments on the tour, and fans rightfully expect to see the world's best compete.
"We are already in discussions with the ATP to ensure this matter received serious consideration."
The Canadian Open takes place before the Cincinnati Open, which is also a Masters 1000 event, and prior to the start of the US Open - the final Grand Slam of the year - on 30 August.
Seven of the existing nine Masters 1000 events - the sport's highest level below the Grand Slams - are now staged over 12 days and concerns over the congested tennis calendar, which stretches across 11 months of the year for the top players, have regularly been voiced.
Britain's Jack Draper and Emma Raducanu recently pulled out of Wimbledon on the eve of their home Grand Slam because of injury.
Draper, who withdrew with a long-term arm injury, said he felt the amount of injuries suffered by leading players is "pretty worrying".
In September 2024, Alcaraz said: "They are going to kill us in some way."
"We firmly believe adjustments are needed in the near future to better protect the integrity of our Masters 1000 events while remaining mindful of the realities players face," added Tetreault.
Earlier this year, women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka and Iga Swiatek pulled out of the Dubai Championships, a WTA 1000 event, two days before it started.
Tournament director Salah Tahlak said players who made late withdrawals from tournaments should be docked points, while Sabalenka said criticism of her was "ridiculous" and that she may not play at the tournament again.
