full_text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, BitMart announced plans to wind down its exchange, Binance revealed it runs monthly phishing simulations against employees and US Ethereum ETFs ended a five-day inflow streak.
BitMart to wind down exchange, end trading by Aug. 26
BitMart will wind down its cryptocurrency exchange, ending all trading services on Aug. 26 before ceasing operations entirely on Jan. 31, 2027.
“After a careful evaluation of the Company’s operating conditions, market environment, and future strategic direction, BitMart has made the difficult decision to commence an orderly wind-down of its trading platform operations,” it said in a Sunday notice.
Under the shutdown plan, BitMart has stopped accepting new user registrations and deposits, while futures trading has entered reduce-only mode and spot markets no longer accept new orders.
BitMart joins a growing list of crypto trading platforms that have announced plans to close shop in recent months. Among them are BitMEX and Dango, which both said this week they would shut down their respective trading platforms.
Binance ‘red teams’ its own staff every month to keep hackers out
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance runs simulated phishing attacks against its own employees and can fire staff who repeatedly fail the tests, according to Binance chief security officer Jimmy Su.
The fake attacks are conducted by Binance’s red team, an internal ethical hacking unit whose job is to break into systems to identify vulnerabilities.
“We do phishing attacks on our own employees on a monthly basis just so we understand if our security hygiene is improving,” Su told Cointelegraph. “The ones that have failed it, we will do remediation training.”
The measure shows the lengths crypto companies will go to prepare for social engineering attacks. Binance, the largest crypto exchange in the world, reports 323 million registered users, while DefiLlama estimates the exchange holds $137.7 billion in assets.
Ethereum ETFs close week in red, end 5-day inflow streak
US-listed spot Ethereum exchange-traded funds (ETFs) logged $70.62 million in net outflows on Friday, ending a five-day inflow streak.
Ethereum funds saw $211.25 million in net inflows over the previous five sessions from July 17 to Thursday, according to SoSoValue data. They still posted $103.9 million in net inflows for the week ended Friday.
Despite the outflows, Ethereum ETFs extended their weekly inflow streak to three straight and have attracted $337.74 million in net inflows so far in July.
Spot crypto ETF flows have become one of the market’s most closely watched gauges of demand for Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) through traditional investment products.
The reversal followed a similar pattern in Bitcoin ETFs, which ended a seven-day inflow streak on Thursday and recorded another $240.08 million in net outflows on Friday.

title: BitMart to wind down trading platform as global CEO says he was not consulted
summary: BitMart's global CEO said the firm told him on July 24 that his employment was ending and that he learned of the closure when it went public.
full_text:
BitMart to wind down trading platform as global CEO says he was not consulted
Quick Take
- BitMart began gradually suspending deposits and new orders late Saturday, will end all trading on Aug. 26 and plans to cease platform operations on Jan. 31, 2027.
- Nenter (Nathan) Chow, BitMart’s global CEO, said the company told him Friday that his employment was being terminated and that he learned of the wind-down when it became public.
- BitMart’s BMX token fell nearly 60% in a day following the announcement.
We'd love your feedback.
Crypto exchange BitMart has begun winding down its trading platform, gradually suspending new registrations, deposits and orders ahead of a full trading halt on Aug. 26.
In a notice published at 9:40 p.m. ET Saturday, the exchange said the decision followed an evaluation of its operating conditions, market environment and future strategic direction.
All spot, futures and other trading services will stop at 01:00 UTC on Aug. 26. BitMart plans to cease trading platform operations at 15:59 UTC on Jan. 31, 2027, after which users will keep login access for a period to view records and submit withdrawal requests.
Withdrawals remain available, with BitMart recommending that users close their positions by 01:00 UTC and submit withdrawal requests by 05:00 UTC on Aug. 26. Requests made after that recommended timeframe will be transferred to a separate processing procedure, while some withdrawals may face additional identity, source-of-funds, sanctions or security reviews.
BitMart also began placing futures accounts in reduce-only mode and stopping the acceptance of new spot orders. Copy trading, grid trading and API trading are being discontinued in phases, along with BitMart Earn, staking, lending and Launchpad products.
BMX, the exchange's token, traded near $0.066 on Sunday morning, down nearly 60% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko data.
CEO says he was not consulted
Following the announcement, global CEO Nenter (Nathan) Chow said on X that the company told him on July 24 that his employment was being terminated and that his offboarding would begin immediately.
Chow said he had played "no role in the management or decision-making of the company" since that date, was not consulted on the wind-down, and learned of it when it became public. He said he had not been given a confirmed final date for his departure and would not comment further.
Chow said his concern is for BitMart's users and employees, and told customers to rely only on the exchange's official channels and to act on the notice without delay. BitMart had not publicly addressed Chow's statement as of publication.
Chow joined BitMart from Animoca Ventures, where he was a partner, and was appointed global CEO in April 2025 when founder Sheldon Xia moved to group president.
Abrupt reversal
The wind-down marks a reversal from BitMart's public messaging earlier this month. In a first-half report, BitMart said assets under management in its asset-management business grew approximately 256% period-over-period, while Chow outlined plans to expand the exchange's prediction markets, tokenized asset offerings and regulatory footprint.
"BitMart is eight years old this year," Chow said in the report. "We intend to be here for the next eight, and we are building accordingly."
Only a month earlier, BitMart said it had secured an Australian Financial Services Licence and planned to expand its local compliance, legal and operations capabilities. At the time, the company said it served more than 13 million users in more than 180 countries and territories. The wind-down announcement did not explain what had changed since either statement.
In a statement dated May 23, BitMart said online claims that users could not withdraw stemmed from its risk system intercepting 239 linked accounts that it accused of farming platform activity subsidies through abusive trading. It said all operations were running normally.
In that statement, BitMart said it would publish a proof-of-reserves report once security and risk-control considerations were addressed. Its website did not appear to contain a subsequent full report as of Sunday, though the exchange previously disclosed several hot-wallet addresses.
BitMart previously suffered a $150 million hot-wallet hack in December 2021. The Block later reported that the exchange's parent company won an arbitration award tied to a separate $6 million attack involving the Bitcoin SV blockchain.
The shutdown comes three days after BitMEX announced that it would close permanently on Sept. 23 following a strategic review. Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao described BitMart's announcement as "tough times (again)" in an X post and said the process appeared to be an orderly wind-down.

title: TechCrunch Mobility: Uber bets on its former CEO
summary: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
full_text:
Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility!
Tesla kicked off earnings season — at least for this sector — and the shareholder letter, along with Elon Musk’s remarks during the conference call, provided some pretty incredible disclosures I imagine have some investors concerned, or at least puzzled.
Tesla has backed off previous promises to reach “volume production” of the Cybercab, Tesla Semi, and Megapack 3 in 2026. And while the company has publicly touted expansions of its Tesla Robotaxi service into new cities in Florida and Texas, the quarter-over-quarter data shows a drop in paid robotaxi miles.
Senior reporter Sean O’Kane took a closer look at a graph shared in Tesla’s shareholder letter. At a passing glance, the chart appears to show steady growth in paid robotaxi rides between August 2025 and June 2026, O’Kane notes. But the numbers displayed are cumulative, and when broken down by quarter, they show that Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet of Model Y SUVs carrying paying passengers covered around 1.1 million miles in the first quarter. That fell to roughly 700,000 miles in the second quarter, a decline of about 36%.
Musk also disclosed during the call that Tesla needs to accumulate driving data specific to the Cybercab before it can put large numbers of the vehicles on the road. That isn’t terribly surprising; the Cybercab is new, after all. But the reason got my attention. He explained that Tesla has to accumulate miles using Cybercabs retrofitted with steering wheels and accelerator and braking pedals so it can calibrate to the Cybercab chassis.
This marks a change from the company’s previous claims. For years, Tesla has said its fleet of nearly 10 million customer cars has been collecting data that could be used to train its advanced driver-assistance system, Full Self-Driving (Supervised), and future robotaxis. Musk’s explanation suggests there is a misalignment between that fleet data and how it’s applied to the Cybercab.
On the financial front, Tesla’s Q2 earnings show a company plowing money into its next generation of products (CapEx has doubled, and the company is back in negative free cash flow territory). And even though revenue is up, the boost wasn’t enough to offset the cost of doing business. The company’s net income fell 5% year over year.
Deals!
Travis Kalanick burst back onto the robotics and mobility scene earlier this year with Atoms — a rebranded holding company atop his ghost kitchen project — and a deal to acquire Anthony Levandowski’s industrial automation startup, Pronto. Now the Uber co-founder and former CEO has $1.7 billion in capital to play with. VC giant Andreessen Horowitz led the round with participation from Bain Capital, Fifth Wall, and Uber. Ben Horowitz will join the company’s board following the investment.
This may seem inconceivable for those who remember Kalanick’s resignation from Uber’s top leadership spot nearly a decade ago — and the string of scandals and lawsuits in the year leading up to his departure. What’s even more incredible is that Uber participated in the funding round. The Information reported Uber invested $100 million into Atoms; conversations I’ve had since confirm that figure and provided new information, including that the investment was made six months ago.
Reminder: In 2016 and while Kalanick was CEO, Uber acquired Levandowski’s self-driving trucks startup Otto. Less than a year later, Levandowski’s former employer Waymo (Google self-driving project) sued Uber for trade secret theft. The companies settled on the fifth day of the trial.
There is a lot of history, much of it messy, between Kalanick and Uber (not to mention Levandowski). But it appears the ride-hailing company is still willing to invest in them.
So what is Atoms going to do with this capital? The details are vague, but a company email from Levandowski suggests that Pronto will be a big part of those plans.
The email states that “Atoms is investing heavily in Industrial AI and physical automation applied to mining and transport.” And later, “Pronto is a core strategic priority for Atoms, and this round is designed to accelerate exactly what matters most to your operations: scaling practical, OEM-agnostic autonomy.”
Other deals that got my attention …
Einride, the Swedish electric and autonomous trucking company, agreed to acquire EV charging startup Flipturn in an all-stock deal worth $38 million.
IBM agreed to buy HRL Laboratories, a quantum computing research lab jointly owned by Boeing and General Motors.
Sila, the battery materials startup, raised $300 million in a round led by Atreides Management and Sutter Hill Ventures with participation from 8VC, Bessemer Venture Partners, Matrix Partners, and funds and accounts advised by T. Rowe Price Associates Inc. The money will be used to expand Sila’s factory in Washington state to produce enough anode material for more than 100,000 EVs.
Notable reads and other tidbits
Aurora had some news this week that didn’t get a ton of attention, but probably should. The company launched its second-generation driverless trucks, which include new hardware that is smaller, as well as upgraded sensor-cleaning systems and extended range lidar — all of which is built for a million-mile service life. The initial fleet will be modest and used on its Dallas-to-Houston route. The fleet will eventually reach 200 driverless trucks by the end of the year and will be used to haul freight for customers like Hirschbach, Uber Freight, McLane, and Detmar, the company said. Importantly for Aurora, these trucks do not have a human observer in the cab.
Ford is turning to Apple for its next generation of EVs. Specifically, Ford is going to integrate Apple Maps navigation and mapping, using a new set of developer tools called MapKit for Automotive, into its new line of electric vehicles, starting with the $30,000 midsize truck in 2027. I asked Ford what this means for Google, which is an existing partner. A company spokesperson told me the Apple announcement “does not change the role of Google Automotive Services across our current and near-term production programs.”
The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety released a study called “Rise of the machines: crash experiences of highly automated vehicles and human drivers.” The organization used a far more clickbaity headline (Waymo’s driverless cars crash less often than people) to direct folks to its work. Unfortunately, that headline misses part of the point. The study does provide evidence that Waymo’s current robotaxis have lower crash involvement rates than human drivers. “Overall, when including police-reportable crashes, Waymo’s crash rate was 68% lower than that of human drivers,” the study reads. It also, importantly, concludes that national-crash and vehicle-miles-traveled data collection for Level 4 vehicles “can be improved for more timely and accurate safety evaluations.”
Mobileye founder and CEO Amnon Shashua plans to step down from the top leadership post after nearly three decades, just as the company pushes into robotaxis and humanoid robots.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration will look into developing new requirements for automakers to ensure drivers and passengers can safely exit their vehicles — the result of a petition that asked the agency to open a safety defect investigation into the emergency mechanical door release design on 2022 Tesla Model 3 vehicles. To be clear, this doesn’t mean there will be new rules.
Rivian has sued the U.S. government for a “full refund” on tariffs paid under President Trump’s “Liberation Day” taxes, which the Supreme Court later ruled unconstitutional.
Two Volkswagen engineers were charged with securities fraud after allegedly profiting off of insider information related to the German automaker’s joint venture with Rivian.

title: Norris wins his first grand prix of year in Hungary
summary: Lando Norris takes his and McLaren's first victory of the year in a compelling Hungarian Grand Prix.
full_text:
Norris wins his first grand prix of year in Hungary
- Published
Lando Norris took his and McLaren's first grand prix victory of the year in a compelling race in Hungary.
As the world champion cruised to a comfortable victory, there was a tense fight for the remaining podium positions in the closing laps between Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli.
Verstappen just managed to hold on while Antonelli took third to extend his championship lead to 50 points over Lewis Hamilton and 59 over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell, who finished seventh after a bad start.
Ferrari's Hamilton finished the grand prix on Antonelli's tail in fourth place but was penalised five seconds for speeding in the pit lane and dropped to fifth behind his team-mate Charles Leclerc.
Norris' team-mate Oscar Piastri led for most of the first half of the race but retired from second place with a gearbox failure.
Norris said he was "happy to be back and be number one again", adding: "My pace today was probably some of the best pace I've ever had. The car was beautiful to drive and I had confidence."
The key stories of the race were:
- Norris' victory, helped by a controversial strategy that did not please his team-mate Piastri 
- A surprise second for Verstappen after a strategy gamble paid off for Red Bull 
- Yet another penalty harming Hamilton's prospects in a disappointing race for Ferrari given their pace 
- A positive weekend for Aston Martin with their new car, despite not scoring points 
Norris and McLaren revive 2025 memories
Norris' concern before the start would have been about the losing a place to Leclerc, who was starting second behind the Briton.
The McLaren driver made a good start, the challenge from Leclerc never materialised, but instead Norris lost the lead to Piastri.
Norris was leading through Turn Two, but a strong start put the Australian second, and when Norris made an error and ran wide through Turn Two, Piastri seized his opportunity to take the lead.
That left McLaren with a quandary for although their cars were running one-two, the slower one was in the lead, and they were concerned about threats from behind.
Piastri led through the first pit stops, with Norris never much more than a second behind, but Norris started to challenge hard in the second stint and wanted to be given the opportunity to challenge his team-mate.
Norris asked to make his second stop first but was refused.
Instead, Piastri was called in, McLaren saying they were covering the threat from Hamilton, who had just stopped himself, and Norris was allowed to run for six further laps before making his pit call for fresh tyres.
Norris returned to the track just in front of Piastri, who had been delayed by a collision with Williams driver Carlos Sainz while lapping the Spaniard, who was penalised five seconds for the incident.
Piastri was clearly unhappy, telling his engineer not to talk to him shortly after Norris returned to the track.
But Norris' pace afterwards justified the decision and he pulled away into a comfortable lead.
Piastri had just been promoted back to second place by Antonelli's second pit stop when he lost use of his gearbox on lap 56 and pulled off after Turn Three.
That led to a late virtual safety car (VSC) which enlivened the battles behind Norris, but he was untouchable as he and McLaren, who came to Hungary with an upgraded car, revived memories of some of their dominant victories of their championship last year.
Verstappen second despite grumbles about car
Verstappen was unhappy with his car for much of the race, with regular complaints on team radio, but Red Bull pulled a masterstroke when they fitted soft tyres to his car at his second pit stop.
The aim was to challenge Hamilton in the later laps after the seven-time champion made an early second stop with 40 laps still to go.
It was heading towards a tense climax when Piastri's retirement brought out the VSC.
That prompted a late round of pit stops, Ferrari bringing in both their drivers and putting them behind Verstappen.
Hamilton came out of the pits and passed Antonelli into the first corner, after the Italian stayed out under the VSC, but had to give the place back after the restart because the Mercedes driver had just passed the key line on the track in front.
Antonelli and Hamilton started chasing back towards Verstappen, but they were delayed while lapping Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto.
That looked as if it might be decisive, but in the end Verstappen was comfortably able to keep Antonelli at bay, crossing the line 3.6 seconds ahead.
Another key point in Verstappen's race had been his re-passing of Hamilton after the Ferrari had got briefly ahead following the first pit stops.
That gave him clear air and enabled the Dutchman to consolidate his race position in third place behind the McLarens, laying the foundations for Red Bull's late strategy call.
Hamilton will leave Hungary ruing another penalty - the one for speeding in the pit lane was his second in two days after behind penalised for blocking Piastri in qualifying, and follows two others at the previous two races in Belgium and Britain.
Behind him, Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was sixth, ahead of Russell, who dropped to 21st place on the first lap after his anti-stall kicked in at the start, and fought back strongly.
At Aston Martin, Lance Stroll finished in 13th, ahead of team-mate Fernando Alonso, their positions dictated to a degree by luck under the VSC and their divergent strategies.
But the key point was that Alonso, in particular, was able to fight with other cars for the first time, and he ran a long first stint on the soft tyres, before switching to the mediums, which was a bold strategy.
The long-awaited upgrade to their car, which was new apart from the front suspension, engine and gearbox, has reduced their lap times by about two seconds.
A Honda engine upgrade is due for the Dutch Grand Prix, the next race in four weeks' time after the summer break, which the team hope will elevate them further and potentially bring the possibility of the occasional points finish into the picture.

Formula 1 is now on its summer holidays with a four-week break before the next race, the Dutch Grand Prix from 21-23 August. It is a sprint event and also F1's final visit to Zandvoort with the circuit's contract ending this year.

title: My entire family went on a boat trip that they never returned from
summary: Peter Watts was just 14 when a pleasure boat disaster killed 15 people, including his entire family.
full_text:
My entire family went on a boat trip that they never returned from
- Published
"It's something you don't get over - you learn to live with it."
Sixty years ago, Peter Watts' entire family was killed in a boating tragedy that shocked the nation.
His nine-year-old sister Angela, 10-year-old brother David, mother Doreen and father Frederick George, along with 11 others, died when the Prince of Wales pleasure boat sank on the Mawddach Estuary in Gwynedd on 22 July, 1966.
Now, a memorial recalling the names of the 15 people who lost their lives has been unveiled.
It was another chance for Peter to travel from the village he grew up in, near Milton Keynes, to the picturesque estuary where the catastrophe unfolded.
"We'd been on holidays in previous years and I'd been on this boat trip [before] and I didn't want to go again," Peter recalled.
Peter was 14 at the time, old enough to be allowed to spend the day on his own in the seaside town of Barmouth, where his family were staying in a boarding house.
The rest of his family joined the queue to board the Prince of Wales for the eight mile (13km) trip down the estuary to the George III Hotel at Penmaenpool.
But the tide pushed the ferry boat into the Penmaenpool toll bridge across the estuary, flinging the 42 passengers into the water as the vessel was wrecked on the bridge.
Local people, including the hotel owner and staff and the toll bridge keeper, ran to the aid of those in the water, managing to pull 27 to safety.
But along with Peter's brother and sister, two other children were among the 15 who could not be saved.
"This happened in the morning, at about 11 in the morning, and I was just waiting hours and hours for them to come back - and they didn't come back," said Peter.
"I went down to the harbour and I heard two people talking about a boat that had sunk. I asked them what was going on, and they said what it was, and I said 'My family is on it' - and they said 'Go to the police station'.
"I sat in there for what seemed ever and a day, and they took the details."
The guest house owners came to take him back, while his aunt and uncle drove up to be with him.
"The next morning we went to Dolgellau to the hospital, where they had found three of them - my mother was still missing," he said.
"My father could swim, but my uncle who identified him said he had had a nasty blow on his head."
It would be another three days before his mother's body was found.
An official inquiry found the boat was carrying six more passengers than the maximum 36 permitted under its certification.
There should also have been two crew members - one on the engine and one on the rudder.
But there was only skipper Edward Llewelyn, 73 at the time, who was found to have acted negligently by a Board of Trade inquiry.
The boat was also short of lifebelts and buoyancy apparatus was stowed away.
Llewelyn was ordered to pay £100 towards the inquiry costs, but no prosecutions were ever brought.
However, the inquiry did lead to changes in the law governing insurance and the number of passengers boats could carry.
The events have left a deep mark on Peter, and the urge to return to Barmouth and the estuary as often as he could.
"If I've ever been anywhere near Wales, even when I've been going to Holyhead, when we went to Ireland, I'd come round this way," he said.
"Just to spend a few minutes."
Returning this time on the 60th anniversary of the tragedy, it was marked with a special memorial and the plaque to remember those who died, unveiled by Dolgellau Town Council.
"Those 15 people - I didn't want them to be forgotten. Having their names there - that's what I wanted," said Peter.

title: Gymnast Reuben Ward goes from Glasgow dreamer to gold medallist
summary: Twelve years ago, a young Reuben Ward watched wide-eyed as Dan Keatings won gymnastics gold for Scotland in Glasgow. Now he celebrates achieving the same feat in the 2026 Commonwealth Games.
full_text:
Gymnast Ward goes from Glasgow dreamer to gold medallist
- Published
Twelve years ago, wee Reuben Ward watched wide-eyed as Dan Keatings won gymnastics gold for Scotland in Glasgow.
That was the day he began dreaming.
In his nine-year-old mind, the notion of competing in the Commonwealth Games for Scotland began to form. Not winning gold. Not even being on a podium. Just pulling on the vest and getting out there.
So when the 21-year-old took the acclaim of an ecstatic Emirates Arena crowd after being announced as the Glasgow 2026 all-around champion, it was all he had ever dreamed of and so much more.
Ward - whose parents Brendan and Lisa left East Kilbride for Bury before he was born - had just become the country's third gold medallist on day three of the Games.
"I remember seeing him win and seeing how it was a big deal to people and I thought 'I want to do that'," Ward told BBC Sport Scotland, recalling Keating's success while in the afterglow of his own.
"So to be here now, having done it myself, is spectacular. It's such a full-circle moment. Glasgow and East Kilbride have been like second homes to me my entire life so to do it here is incredibly special."
'I'm just so overwhelmed, man'
There was a sense beforehand that Ward could contend here. A bronze maybe. Perhaps even a silver depending how things go.
His team-mates privately made noises that, should everything fall in his favour, gold could be within reach. They had seen him in training, and performed alongside him in the team event on Friday, where Scotland finished fourth.
They knew he was in a good place.
Ward sat seventh after the floor exercise, but streaked into the lead after a splendid performance on the pommel - routinely his strongest event.
He retained that advantage after the rings - by which point assorted Team Scotland officials and members of the Scottish media had arrived in dribs and drabs, with the sniff of a gold in the air.
Ward's vault had been compromised in the team event by a slight issue in his run up - he had to adapt it on the fly and could only execute two twists - but he nailed it this time, performing three to go into the final two rotations top of the standings.
A strong showing in the parallel bars - and a judicious Team Scotland appeal to add an extra 0.100 - maintained his lead at 0.550, meaning he needed to keep his shape in the horizontal bar to clinch gold.
Ward did that and more.
As he stuck his landing, his coach Jake Seager fell to his knees celebrating before the two embraced. It wasn't official yet, but they knew.
"I like to imagine the best scenario possible and that was winning," added Ward when asked what he was thinking as his head hit the pillow on Saturday night.
"It kept me awake a little bit because I was picturing it and feeling the emotions. But this beat the expectations by a mile.
"Falling short on Friday was heartbreaking and I'm just so overwhelmed, man. I can barely put words together."
It could get even better. He goes on the floor and pommel on Monday, and is a real medal contender in the later.
His celebrations will have to wait for now, but by Tuesday, Ward could well be getting up to all sorts of capers in Glasgow with his Scotland team-mates.
"Tonight looks like eating hotel food and probably getting a pretty bad night's sleep," he said. "Then I'll come in tomorrow, and try to relax and hit my routine.
"On Tuesday, after the competition, I'll celebrate big time with the team, with my boys. I love them so much and them coming to see me at the end when I was going around of the arena was special.
"I'm hoping we'll get to experience a bit of Glasgow.. "

title: Emmerdale makers seek forever home for soap village
summary: The company behind the TV drama asks to make permanent the site of its current set in Leeds.
full_text:
Emmerdale makers seek forever home for soap village
- Published
The makers of TV drama Emmerdale hope to continue filming on their village set at a site in Leeds after seeking permission from the council.
ITV Studios has applied to Leeds City Council to remain at the farm site in Harewood which the show has occupied since 1997.
Current planning permission allows for the location, which includes the Woolpack pub and Burden Head Farm, to be used until next year.
If granted, consent from council planners would allow the site, which is popular with tourists, to be used on a permanent basis.
A planning report said the set provided a variety of exterior views and was used for more than 260 episodes each year.
It said: "The Emmerdale Village Production Set provides a facility which adapts to the ever-changing needs of production.
"These could be planned changes for certain storylines or even immediate changes due to weather conditions, cast availability or other scheduling challenges."
ITV said continued use of the set was needed to depict farming life and the Yorkshire countryside, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service.
Interior and exterior scenes were filmed at the Harewood site, while studio space on Kirkstall Road was used for some indoor sets, including the Woolpack.
The report said: "Emmerdale Village was designed to include everything a typical rural village would have, including a village hall, café, church, residential dwellings and more."
Current planning permission would expire on 3 June 2027, with a condition requiring the site to be restored to its original condition within six months.
A full planning application is out for consultation until 13 August.

title: 'It was like a movie - I looked up and an exploded barn rained on me'
summary: Photographer Scott Johnson's studio is close to where a fire triggered a massive explosion.
full_text:
'It was like a movie - I looked up and an exploded barn rained on me'
- Published
"I closed the door, and then the explosion happened, and it threw me against the door - everything was raining down on me," says Scott Johnson.
The wedding photographer had just walked out of his studio at Highlands Farm, near Rettendon, Essex, when a fire caused a huge explosion at the industrial estate.
The fire service declared a major incident on Friday as more than 100 firefighters tackled the flames. Twenty firefighters were taken to hospital and have since been discharged.
It was like "witnessing something that is literally out of a movie", said Johnson, adding it was a miracle he was unscathed except for "some really nasty tinnitus".
The photographer was driving to his studio for a meeting when he realised the fire on the horizon was at the farm where it was based.
"It was about 150 metres (492ft) from my front door, and I quickly cancelled the meeting and thought, 'I'm not happy with where the wind is going on this'," he said.
Johnson began removing some of his more expensive kit from the studio and was putting it in the van when the explosion took place.
A unit housing fertiliser had exploded.
He said: "It blew me into the door and I just ran to the van, dropped the bit I went back in for - maybe it saved my life, I don't know."
As it happened: Twenty firefighters taken to hospital after major Essex explosion
The photographer was shocked to see his studio roof had completely caved in.
Having driven to a safe distance, "I pulled over, and I was just in shock and started to shake", he said, although he was reassured after an ambulance crew checked him over.
Johnson managed to cover his wedding booking on Saturday, praising his "amazing assistant" James Musselwhite for driving from Portsmouth to help him out.
"I'm in a little bit of shock still, to be honest," he said.
"I'm completely unscathed apart from a bit of a dodgy ear from the pressure - but how I've got away with it unscathed I have no idea."
Rick Hylton, the county's chief fire officer, described the incident as "one of the most challenging and complex incidents Essex County Fire and Rescue Service has responded to in recent years".
Throughout Saturday evening, crews were tackling small fires, which had spread due to the wind, in neighbouring fields.
About 15 firefighters remained on the scene overnight to dampen down hotspots and monitor the area.
Station Manager Paul Champ said: "We'd like to thank the local community for their continued patience while we've been working with partners to make the area safe.
"Recovery information for residents and businesses will be coordinated by Chelmsford City Council."
An investigation into the cause of the fire has begun.
The UK Health Security Agency confirmed the risk to health from the debris and smoke plume was low.

title: Lando Norris wins Hungarian Grand Prix for first F1 triumph in 2026
summary: Defending champion Norris wins his first race of the year as Verstappen finishes second, and leader Antonelli third.
full_text:
Lando Norris wins Hungarian Grand Prix for first F1 triumph in 2026
Defending champion Norris wins his first race of the year as Verstappen finishes second and leader Antonelli is third.
Lando Norris has ended an eight-month wait for a Formula One victory with strong pace and a dose of good fortune to win the Hungarian Grand Prix on Sunday.
McLaren’s defending champion finished ahead of Max Verstappen in Red Bull and teenage sensation Kimi Antonelli at the Hungaroring circuit in Budapest on Sunday.
Norris was on pole but lost the lead to his McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri when he ran wide at the second corner, before reclaiming the lead after Piastri was delayed by a collision with Carlos Sainz Jr during a lap.
This allowed Norris to come out of the pits ahead of his teammate and cruise to a win.
“The car was unbelievable today. Well done guys, incredible. We were flying,” Norris said. “Nice to finally be able to do it all for you. Feels like it’s been a while.”
Piastri then stopped with a broken gearbox, paving the way for Verstappen to take second, with Antonelli third.
Antonelli increased his standings lead, with title rival Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth after a penalty for speeding in the pits and George Russell seventh after a near-stall at the start.
Norris hadn’t won a full Grand Prix race since Sao Paulo in November, though he did win a sprint in Miami in May.
Hungary was the last race before the mid-season break. The next race is the Dutch Grand Prix on August 23.

title: More than 360,000 evacuated as wildfires rage in France and Spain
summary: French and Spanish authorities are struggling to contain the blazes, which are partly caused by successive heatwaves.
full_text:
More than 360,000 evacuated as wildfires rage in France and Spain
French and Spanish authorities are struggling to contain the blazes, with teams lacking capacity and resources.
Blazes raging in parts of France and Spain show no sign of abating and have forced more than 360,000 people to leave their homes, after successive stifling summer heatwaves created the ideal conditions for wildfires to thrive.
In France’s southwestern Gironde region, 55,000 people were evacuated overnight, officials said on Sunday. France is among the worst-affected countries in Europe, with around 42,000 hectares (103,780 acres) of land in Gironde alone already burned in one of the largest wildfires the country has endured since the Second World War. So far, some 250,000 people have been evacuated from the region..

- list 2 of 3Wildfires in Spain and France force evacuation of more than 267,000 people
- list 3 of 3Tour de France final stage shortened as emergency teams tackle wildfires
The flames are advancing towards the famous wine-growing port city of Bordeaux. Its mayor, Thomas Cazenave, said in a post on X that the city was “prepared to welcome in the best possible conditions all the evacuated individuals who have no backup housing solution”.
The blazes in Europe have renewed questions about the impact of climate change.
The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has said that last month was the hottest June in western Europe on record and the second-warmest globally. Both Germany and the UK broke temperature records for three straight days.
French and Spanish firefighters are struggling to contain the blazes, with teams in some areas lacking the capacity and resources to respond efficiently. The situation has triggered concerns about how authorities will deal with future wildfires, which are likely to worsen as temperatures continue to increase.
Since the blazes broke out on Tuesday, some 1,500 military personnel have been deployed by French authorities, along with 1,700 security personnel and 1,400 firefighters. Military planes have also been used to drop flame retardants.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Saturday that five aircraft and two helicopters had been dispatched to France by the European Union.
Neighbouring Spain has declared a national emergency, with more than 116,000 people having been evacuated due to fires west of Madrid and in the east coast region of Valencia. Firefighters there found an elderly man dead inside his car on Saturday.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has said around 130,000 hectares of land have already been burned in the country this year, warning that there are “complex times ahead”.

title: Tunisia grapples with five years of crisis since Saied’s power grab
summary: Tunisians protest five years of President Kais Saied's rule amid economic crisis and political arrests.
full_text:
Tunisia grapples with five years of crisis since Saied’s power grab
Thousands protest, political prisoners languish, and US lawmakers threaten sanctions as Tunisia marks five years of Saied’s rule.
Five years after Tunisian President Kais Saied suspended parliament and attained sweeping powers, the country remains sharply divided, grappling with a severe economic downturn and a worsening political deadlock.
Saied’s supporters continue to view the measures taken by him in July 2021 – when he suspended parliament and dismissed Prime Minister Hichem Mechichi – as a necessary “correction” to save the country. The opposition says that since then, state institutions have collapsed, promises have gone unfulfilled, and there has been an unprecedented concentration of power in his hands.
Speaking to Al Jazeera’s Ma Waraa al-Khabar (Behind the News) programme, political and economic experts debated the legacy of Saied’s five-year rule, painting a picture of an economy hindered by a poor business climate, populist policies, and a lack of clear vision.
An economy in free fall
Since Saied assumed near-total control of the levers of power five years ago, Tunisia’s economic indicators have largely plummeted.
Ridha Chkoundali, an economics professor at the University of Tunisia, said that the investment rate in the country has dropped from an average of 20 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) between 2015 and 2019 to just 8 percent in 2023.
Chkoundali attributed this sharp decline to an environment that drives away investment, exacerbated by a significant burden from taxes, which have risen by five percentage points since 2015.
Taxation, he argued, is no longer used to stimulate investment but simply to collect revenues at the expense of economic growth.
The crisis has hit ordinary Tunisians the hardest. Food inflation has reached nearly three times the general average, severely eroding purchasing power. Meanwhile, unemployment has surged, particularly among university graduates, pushing many to leave the country for better economic opportunities abroad.
Mohamed Abbou, a former minister of state and former secretary-general of the Democratic Current party, argued that the crisis is rooted in Saied’s style of governance, adding that the rule of law has been replaced by a climate of intimidation and threats.
“Tunisia has lost all credibility,” Abbou said. “Everyone fears the situation in Tunisia because there is no rationality… there is no stability in laws, taxes, or anything else.”
Abbou particularly criticised Saied’s approach to international finance, pointing out that the president rejected a deal with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) purely to maintain a populist image. At the same time, he quietly implemented many of the IMF’s harsh austerity demands, such as halting public sector hiring and reducing imports.
However, supporters of the current government argue that it is unfair to blame Saied’s administration entirely for an economic crisis that predates his rule.
Political analyst Souhaib Mezrigui says the current situation is the result of an absence of any clear economic or social vision over the past 10 years. He placed blame for the current crisis squarely on the political class that has ruled Tunisia since the 2011 revolution.
Protests and political prisoners
Tunisia’s economic stagnation has manifested into tangible anger on the streets. Coinciding with the five-year anniversary, thousands of Tunisians rallied in the capital’s Habib Bourguiba Avenue on Saturday, protesting against deteriorating living conditions, rolling water and electricity cuts, and a backsliding in democracy.
Organised by a coalition of opposition parties and the “Nafas” civil initiative, the crowds called for Saied to “leave” and revived the 2011 democratic revolution’s rallying cry: “The people want the fall of the regime”.
A central demand of the protests was the release of political prisoners, who have filled Tunisia’s jails since Saied began his crackdown on dissent. Among the most prominent detainees is Rached Ghannouchi, the 85-year-old former parliament speaker and Ennahdha leader, who was recently sentenced to life in prison.
Ghannouchi’s health has rapidly deteriorated in detention. He recently fainted in Mornaguia prison, where temperatures reportedly reached 52 degrees Celsius (126 degrees Fahrenheit). Rights groups and families of detainees, such as opposition politician Ahmed Nejib Chebbi, have repeatedly warned about the dire conditions inside the detention facility and the toll it is taking on elderly inmates.
Imed al-Khamiri, a spokesman for the Ennahdha party, told Al Jazeera that the continued detention of political figures and opposition leaders remains a “disgrace to the Tunisian state”.
US lawmaker calls for sanctions
Saied’s consolidation of power has also drawn renewed international condemnation. Marking the anniversary, US Representative Joe Wilson issued a scathing statement, accusing Saied of transforming the Arab world’s only constitutional democracy into a “one-man dictatorship”.
Wilson accused the Tunisian regime of phenomenally increasing corruption, destroying opportunities for the youth, and shifting its alliances to become a close associate of Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iran, and Hezbollah.
Noting that Saied’s government has even jailed US citizens, Wilson urged the US State Department to issue a “Level 4: Do Not Travel” advisory for Tunisia.
“I will also continue to work to pass the Tunisia Democracy Restoration Act imposing sanctions on Saied and his inner circle,” Wilson stated on the social media platform X, adding: “Democracy in Tunisia will win in the end. Madmen tyrants will not last.”

title: ‘Get rid of them’: One Nation senator claims party will ‘remigrate’ illegal visa holders in resurfaced interview
summary:
Exclusive: Malcolm Roberts uses white supremacist concept to describe the party’s plans for deporting 200,000 people from Australia

Senator Malcolm Roberts claims One Nation wants to deport at least 200,000 people and has repeatedly referred to the far-right concept of “remigration” in podcast interviews and speeches to niche platforms.

In two recent podcasts, Roberts said One Nation wanted to deport 100,000 temporary residents as well as 100,000 international students – a total much higher than the party’s published policy. The senator said after those people were removed, he wanted to “start working on the higher numbers of people we need to get rid of”.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Senator Malcolm Roberts claims One Nation wants to deport at least 200,000 people and has repeatedly referred to the far-right concept of “remigration” in podcast interviews and speeches to niche platforms.
In two recent podcasts, Roberts said One Nation wanted to deport 100,000 temporary residents as well as 100,000 international students – a total much higher than the party’s published policy. The senator said after those people were removed, he wanted to “start working on the higher numbers of people we need to get rid of”.
One Nation’s policy website states the party would seek to “deport 75,000 illegal migrants”, specifically noting “visa overstayers, illegal workers, and unlawful non-residents”. The website also pledges to “end the student visa loopholes that turn study into a backdoor to permanent residency or low-wage labour”.
But Roberts, in an interview with the 2 Worlds Collide podcast in November 2025, suggested One Nation wanted to deport or “remigrate” a far higher number.
“We would also deport immediately anybody who’s here illegally, and that’s 100,000 people now … on contravention of their resident visas. That’s 100,000 we would deport, remigrate. Call it what you want. Get rid of them straight away,” he said.
“Then we’ve got about an estimated 100,000 international students who are here illegally. They’ve either graduated and not gone home or they’ve breached their legal visa. So we would send them home.”
In another interview with podcaster Brodie Buchal, published in June, Roberts repeated those sentiments.
“We have 100,000 people here on temporary resident visas illegally. We would deport them, remigrate them, send them home,” he said.
“We’ve got 100,000 students who are here illegally, and we suspect it’s much, much more. Send them home.”
“We’d tighten the entry requirements, remigrate, deport, and then start working on the higher numbers of people we need to get rid of.”
One Nation was contacted for comment and clarification of its deportation policy.
One Nation’s hardline immigration policy has come under renewed scrutiny after Pauline Hanson’s appearance on Channel Seven’s Spotlight program, where she met Rupert Lowe, leader of hard-right party Restore Britain. Lowe gave her a pamphlet titled “mass deportations” and Hanson replied they were “on the same page”.
Seven reporter Liam Bartlett asked Hanson whether she thought “this concept of mass deportation is a good one?” She replied: “I love it.”
However One Nation has consistently declined to detail how it would enact such a policy. MP Barnaby Joyce on Monday said people would be deported “as it becomes apparent that they’re not supposed to be here”, including “as people present themselves for medical issues”.
Abul Rizvi, former deputy secretary of the immigration department, said it would be “eyewateringly expensive” for a system to deport such numbers of people from Australia, or a Trump-style mass deportation operation like the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). He said recent figures showed only about 2,000 people were apprehended, detained and deported from Australia last year, with another 6,000 voluntarily leaving.
“It would cost a fortune and unless you did it carefully, it would result in massive errors and all sorts of problems,” Rizvi said.
“There is a sensible policy in this space to be developed, but you need to do it in a careful, well-targeted way that doesn’t increase in huge errors, huge numbers of people detained and clogging up court systems.”
Roberts’ recent comments have also repeatedly referenced “remigration”. The term has featured in Trump administration immigration policies, including an “office of remigration” to oversee deportations and “voluntary return of migrants” – Trump himself tweeted about his plan to return “illegal migrants to their home countries (also known as remigration)”.
But remigration has also become a buzzword for the global far right. The Global Project Against Hate and Extremism described remigration as “a white supremacist policy concept that calls for the forced removal of immigrants, refugees, and their descendants — including legal residents and citizens — based on race, ethnicity, culture, being perceived as ‘non-white,’ or a failure to ‘assimilate’.”
One Nation was contacted for comment regarding Roberts’ understanding of the term.
In addition to mentioning “remigration” on the 2 Worlds Collide and Brodie Buchal podcasts, Roberts also advocated for it during a speech to a conference organised by conservative campaign group Firebrand. Photos from that conference, posted to social media, show Hanson was also in attendance.
The conference host, welcoming Roberts onto the stage, praised him as “one of the only MPs yet to mention the magical, unmentionable word ‘remigration’”.
In his address, Roberts said: “Remigration is the second part of my my speech. Take the people who are not fitting in or that we don’t need and send them home.
“We need to put Australia first. Stop immigration, deport people, remigrate.”
In that speech, Roberts said he was “opposed to mass immigration, the swamping of our culture” but was “not opposed to immigrants”.
Roberts’ speech was praised by a white supremacist news outlet, The Noticer. The outlet said “remigration” had been popularised by German and Austrian far-right parties and activists, who frame the term as meaning the mass removal of non-white citizens.
Dr Kurt Sengul, a research fellow at Macquarie University who studies far-right ideology, called remigration “an extreme and dangerous” position.
“It’s important to note that remigration refers to the forced repatriation of all non-white people, not just so-called illegal or undocumented migrants or reducing ‘mass migration’. It’s an extreme position rooted in ethnic cleansing and white supremacy,” he said.
Asked if he thought there was any other way to interpret the term “remigration” in this context, Sengul said no.
“I don’t think there is any other way to see it; there’s not a friendlier or more moderate version of remigration … it sends a powerful signal to far-right activists that One Nation are embracing the term,” he said.

title: Israeli siblings who fear breaking law in Gaza under IDF owed protection by Australia, tribunal finds
summary:
Exclusive: Tribunal accepts three siblings could face ‘persecution’ for refusing military conscription due to their political opinion on war

Three Israeli citizens facing conscription into the Israel Defense Forces have been granted the right to reapply for protection visas in Australia, after a government tribunal found they held a genuine fear they would be forced to break international humanitarian law in Gaza.

The Administrative Review Tribunal found the punishment the young adults could face from the state of Israel – including imprisonment as conscientious objectors – would amount to persecution.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Three Israeli citizens facing conscription into the Israel Defense Forces have been granted the right to reapply for protection visas in Australia, after a government tribunal found they held a genuine fear they would be forced to break international humanitarian law in Gaza.
The Administrative Review Tribunal found the punishment the young adults could face from the state of Israel – including imprisonment as conscientious objectors – would amount to persecution.
Part of a family group, three siblings faced mandatory national service if they were returned to Israel, and held a genuine belief they would be forced to “engage in breaches of international humanitarian law”.
The tribunal found there were “credible allegations that Israel’s military operations in the Gaza Strip are in breach of international humanitarian law” and that international opinion was that the IDF’s actions in Gaza were disproportionate. It found the three siblings were refugees facing persecution from the state of Israel, and Australia had a legal obligation to protect them.
The family’s case went before the tribunal in October last year. The decision was published in March.
The family – a husband and wife and their children – arrived in Australia on the husband’s working visa a decade ago.
That visa expired, and the family applied for protection visas in 2024, six months after the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023 sparked the current conflict in Gaza and Israel. Their application for protection was rejected by the government.
On appeal to the tribunal, the family claimed they were not safe from terrorist attacks anywhere in Israel and had “lost faith in the ability of the state of Israel to protect its citizens”, citing previous terrorist attacks by Hamas and being forced to live in bunkers for sustained periods.
This argument was not accepted by the tribunal. While the tribunal found the family was at risk of being injured or killed by a Hamas rocket attack, it said any harm they suffered would not be the result of “discriminatory conduct aimed at them”.
“Rather, it would be because they were a casualty of the armed conflict between Israel and Hamas. The applicants do not meet the refugee criterion in relation to this aspect of their claims.”
However, the couple’s eldest child – who, along with two siblings, had reached the age of 18 – told the tribunal she and her siblings had vowed to refuse the national service compulsory for Israeli citizens.
“She gave evidence that she and [her two siblings] had made a pact between themselves that they would refuse to serve in the Israel Defence Forces (the IDF).
“The basis of their refusal to serve in the IDF was that they would be required to serve in the Israel-Palestinian conflict on the Gaza Strip, and as part of that conflict may be forced to engage in breaches of international humanitarian law. The tribunal accepts that these views are genuinely held.”
The tribunal said it accepted that the three adult siblings “would be liable to terms of imprisonment of up to two years for refusing to serve in the IDF”.
The tribunal noted that arrest warrants had been issued by the international criminal court against the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, and the former defence minister Yoav Gallant on allegations of war crimes and crimes against humanity, including murder.
The tribunal also noted the United Nations Commission of Inquiry had reported that “Israel authorities and Israeli security forces have committed and are continuing to commit genocide against the Palestinians in the Gaza Strip”.
“The International Criminal Court arrest warrant and the United Nations Commission of Inquiry report contain credible allegations that Israel’s military operations in the Gaza Strip are in breach of international humanitarian law,” the tribunal said.
“This is a situation where Israel’s military operations are not currently considered by the international community to be proportionate in the means used to achieve a legitimate national objective of Israel.”
The tribunal said it was not required to express any “concluded views” as to whether Israel had engaged in acts of genocide and noted Netanyahu and Gallant were “entitled to a presumption of innocence” before the ICC.
The tribunal argued that the enforcement of Israel’s national service laws – and the expected punishment for refusing to serve – “would amount to persecution” of the adult siblings in the family.
“The tribunal is satisfied that the risk of imprisonment faced by the [siblings] for refusal to do military service would involve a real chance of serious harm to them. The essential and significant reason for this persecution would be the political opinion underlying their refusal to do compulsory military service.
“There are no reasonable steps the [siblings] could take to modify their behaviour to avoid the threat of serious harm. As the risk of persecution comes from the state itself, the tribunal finds that state protection is not available. The risk of harm also extends to all areas of Israel.”
The tribunal ruled the three adult siblings facing conscription into the IDF met Australia’s obligations for protection under the refugees convention: that is, they faced a “well-founded fear of persecution” in their home country. The entire family should be afforded protection, the tribunal found.
The tribunal ordered that the family’s application for protection visas be reconsidered.
The Guardian sought comment from the Department of Home Affairs.

title: Berlin Pride van and knife rampage an ‘Islamist terrorist attack’, say German authorities
summary:
Hunt ongoing for main suspect, named as Abdul Ballout, 21, after fatal attack in Tiergarten park close to LGBTQ+ event

A deadly van ramming and knife rampage near Berlin’s Pride festival was an Islamist terrorist attack, German authorities have said, with a hunt ongoing to find the main suspect.

One person was killed and 29 were injured after a man drove a minivan into a crowd of pedestrians, then stabbed people with what appeared to be a machete. The attack took place in the Tiergarten park near the Brandenburg Gate at around 10pm local time on Saturday, close to one of Europe’s biggest LGBTQ+ celebrations.

Continue reading...
full_text:
A deadly van ramming and knife rampage near Berlin’s Pride festival was an Islamist terrorist attack, German authorities have said, with a hunt ongoing to find the main suspect.
One person was killed and 29 were injured after a man drove a minivan into a crowd of pedestrians, then stabbed people with what appeared to be a machete. The attack took place in the Tiergarten park near the Brandenburg Gate at around 10pm local time on Saturday, close to one of Europe’s biggest LGBTQ+ celebrations.
The German interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, named the chief suspect as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, and said Ballout was thought to have used a machete to attack people, leaving some victims with life-threatening injuries. “Everything we see here indicates that we are dealing with an Islamist terrorist attack,” Dobrindt said.
“We are dealing here with a suspected perpetrator, who had previously drawn attention to himself through a high volume of criminal offences, radicalisation and affiliation with the Islamist scene,” Dobrindt told a press conference near the site of the attack. He said Ballout had a criminal conviction and had been sentenced to a year and 10 months in jail, but that the sentence had been suspended.
German media reported that Ballout, a German national with Lebanese roots, was a supporter of Islamic State and last year travelled to the Middle East in a failed attempt to join the group. He was then convicted in Germany of “preparing a serious act of subversive violence”, the Bild and Spiegel newspapers reported.
Police and prosecutors have asked for help in finding Ballout, but warned the public to avoid “direct contact” with him, saying he may be armed and dangerous.
Police described Ballout as thin, about 1.90 metres (6ft 3in) tall with black hair, and dressed in a black hoodie and white trousers.
Police searched an apartment in the Schöneberg district of Berlin in the early hours of Sunday, but said they had found no one there.
The chancellor, Friedrich Merz, urged Germany to avoid division and intimidation in the wake of the attack. “We will think about consequences, we will defend our freedom,” he said in a news conference.
Earlier Merz vowed to punish those responsible, describing the “heinous act” as an “attack on our society” in a social media post. The flag at the German Bundestag was ordered to be lowered to half mast.
The attack forced organisers to cut short one of Europe’s largest Pride events and came as Germany remains on edge after a series of deadly vehicle and knife attacks.
Hours after the attack many details remained unclear, but police said the vehicle had struck multiple people after charging into the Tiergarten close to the Brandenburg Gate. Police said those hurt “included several with life-threatening injuries”.
The driver of the white minivan had swerved shortly before 10pm into the Tiergarten, close to where the route of the Pride march had been earlier in the day, hitting people on a path and crashing into a tree, police said.
“[The vehicle] was empty, which is why we are currently working intensively to track down the perpetrator or perpetrators,” police said. The tabloid newspaper Bild cited a witness as saying that a man had emerged from the vehicle and fled on foot.
A hunt involving helicopters and officers from several German states was under way across the capital on Sunday.
Emergency workers set up a helicopter landing pad near the Reichstag parliament building to transport the injured to hospitals.
Julian Methig, who attended the event, described it as a terrible day. “It’s one of the worst days for the queer community and a day I personally hoped I’d never have to experience … I’m shocked.”
Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered in the German capital in warm summer sunshine to celebrate the pride parade.
It is known in Germany as Christopher Street Day (CSD), named after the site of the Stonewall Inn in New York City where riots against police raids touched off the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement. CSD was first held in West Berlin in 1979.
Berlin’s mayor, Kai Wegner, called the deadly assault “an attack on our free and cosmopolitan society”.
“Following a peaceful and colourful CSD, the rally for a tolerant and peaceful Berlin was attacked in the most brutal manner,” he said on X. “Berlin is the city of freedom – and our freedom has today been attacked in the most appalling way. My thoughts are with the victims, their families and friends.”
For the first time in its history, CSD began on Friday night this year with a pro-democracy political rally. Berlin will hold a state election in September.
The parade on Saturday ran under the motto “taking a stand is hot” which organisers said was “in response to increasing hostility” to queer people in Germany.
More than 80 floats and 50 groups on foot joined the procession through the city centre past Potsdamer Platz and the Victory Column monument in the Tiergarten, culminating in a rally at the Brandenburg Gate.
Earlier in the day one person was arrested for resisting police orders at a far-right counterprotest.
Before last year’s parade, Berlin LGBTQ+ organisations sounded the alarm that attacks had become more frequent while hard-won rights were under threat. Campaigners said a rise in hostility had accompanied the surge in support for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland party, now the most popular party in national opinion polls, as well as an increase in Islamist-inspired attacks.
European leaders offered solidarity, including heads of government in Belgium, the Netherlands and Sweden. “Italy firmly condemns and opposes all forms of hate and extremism,” the prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, wrote on X, adding: “We stand with Germany and the German people.” The French president, Emmanuel Macron, said: “Faced with hatred and violence, our response will always be unity, freedom, and resolve.”
The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, a German centre-right politician allied with Merz, sent her deepest sympathy to the victims of the attack, describing the CSD parade as standing for “freedom, dignity and equality – the fundamental values of the EU”.
The UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said he was “horrified by the appalling attack in Berlin” and had spoken to his counterpart, Johann Wadephul, “to convey the UK’s solidarity: we stand with Germany”.
Far-right leaders were also quick to comment on the attacks. The co-leader of the Alternative für Deutschland Tino Chrupalla wrote on X: “We will not allow religious extremists to divide our country with violence and intolerance!”
The president of France’s National Rally, Jordan Bardella, wrote: “The Islamist threat remains a major issue in Europe and continues to target what they hate most about our civilisation – and what we cherish so much – freedom.”

title: Joy in Greece as Mount Olympus joins Unesco list of world heritage sites
summary:
Mythical home of the ancient Greek gods designated alongside the D-day landing beaches in Normandy

After a 12-year wait, Mount Olympus, the mythical home of the ancient Greek gods, has been inducted into a hall of more modern fame as Unesco announced it would be added to its world heritage list.

Greece’s highest mountain made the list alongside the second world war D-day landing beaches in northern France and the ancient Japanese capitals of Asuka and Fujiwara. South Sudan’s Boma-Badingilo landscape, host to one of the world’s largest land mammal migrations, also won a designation – a first for the east African country.

Continue reading...
full_text:
After a 12-year wait, Mount Olympus, the mythical home of the ancient Greek gods, has been inducted into a hall of more modern fame as Unesco announced it would be added to its world heritage list.
Greece’s highest mountain made the list alongside the second world war D-day landing beaches in northern France and the ancient Japanese capitals of Asuka and Fujiwara. South Sudan’s Boma-Badingilo landscape, host to one of the world’s largest land mammal migrations, also won a designation – a first for the east African country.
The nominations were among dozens reviewed at a Unesco committee meeting in Busan, South Korea, on Sunday.
In the case of Olympus, inscribed as a mixed world heritage site in recognition of its cultural and natural significance, the news was met with near euphoria in Greece.
Immortalised as the seat of Zeus, king of the 12 Olympian deities, the mountain rising 2,918 metres from a base near sea level had been on a tentative list of sites since 2014.
The head of Greece’s Unesco delegation in Busan, Georgios Koumoutsakos, hailed the decision as one that would ensure the site’s preservation.
“It reaffirms our unwavering commitment to safeguarding Mount Olympus for the benefit of present and future generations,” he said. “As Greek mythology wisely reminds us, it is always best to remain on good terms with the gods.”
The region’s mayor, Evangelos Geroliolios, said before the announcement that the site’s induction would “place greater responsibility on our part to protect the [local] environment”, not least its extraordinary biodiversity.
The committee’s annual meeting, which ends on Wednesday, is expected to examine about 30 nominations. Those successful will join 1,248 sites across 170 countries admitted to the world heritage list for their “outstanding value to humanity”.
Inscribed monuments can provide a vital boost for their preservation under an international convention overseen by Unesco, which also gives advice and financial support. Other world heritage sites include the Acropolis in Athens, the Great Wall of China, the pyramids of Giza in Egypt and the Taj Mahal in India.
As with Mount Olympus, efforts to get the D-day beaches in Normandy inscribed had gone back years.
Included in the French bid were all five of the beaches – Omaha, Utah, Sword, Gold and Juno – where more than 150,000 allied troops came ashore on 6 June 1944, and the Pointe du Hoc cliff that was also a focal point of the assault.
The largest amphibious operation ever mounted, in which 4,000 soldiers died, was decisive in the battle to liberate Europe from Nazi occupation.
France first nominated the 50-mile (80km) stretch of coastline in 2008. Reacting to the decision, the country’s permanent delegate to Unesco, Ahlem Gharbi, said the designation carried particular weight at a time of such international tensions.
The president of the Normandy region, Hervé Morin, who had championed the cause, maintained that inclusion on the list would represent “immense recognition” for the soldiers who had sacrificed so much to defeat Nazism.
Echoing Greek officials, he said: “This decision places a responsibility upon us. It compels us to preserve this site, to protect it, to cherish it even more, and to promote its value.”
The international council on monuments and sites, one of the bodies that recommends additions to the Unesco list, had previously warned of the threat posed to the Normandy sites by tourism, climate change, rising sea levels and nearby windfarm development, and had called for stronger monitoring and preservation.
The coastline is covered with extensive remnants of the time of the landings, including concrete German bunkers and gun positions, sunken vessels and allied installations.
Unesco said in a statement that the beaches formed an “exceptional cultural landscape shaped both by the events of 1944 and by their enduring remembrance”, all of which justified further protection. As with Mount Olympus, the landing points have attracted record numbers of tourists in recent years.
The agency’s move to include places associated with conflict has fuelled controversial debate over whether “sites of memory” are befitting of world heritage status and Unesco’s stated mission to “foster a world of greater equality and peace”.
Three sites used by Cambodia’s Khmer Rouge regime for torture and execution were inscribed last year.
After so many years of campaigning, Greek officials said Sunday’s decision had been made all the sweeter given signs of further delays.
In the draft agenda of this week’s meeting, Unesco had signalled the Mount Olympus file would be referred back to the country for further details, spurring fears that proved to be baseless when the nomination won unanimous support.

title: Romania summons Russia’s ambassador after downing third drone since Friday
summary:
F-16 fighter jet intercepted drone in Romanian airspace over Black Sea, defence minister says

Romania has said it is summoning Russia’s ambassador after the Nato member’s military shot down a third drone in as many days.

Romania has experienced frequent drone incursions since Russia launched its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, but had not shot down any until Friday.

Continue reading...
full_text:
Romania has said it is summoning Russia’s ambassador after the Nato member’s military shot down a third drone in as many days.
Romania has experienced frequent drone incursions since Russia launched its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, but had not shot down any until Friday.
On Sunday, a Romanian F-16 fighter jet shot down a drone over the Black Sea, five minutes after it entered the country’s airspace, Romania’s defence minister, Radu Miruță, said on Facebook.
The foreign minister, Oana Țoiu, said Romania was summoning Russia’s ambassador after “repeated violations”.
The Romanian president, Nicușor Dan, said that according to an investigation, a drone shot down on Friday was a “Shahed model used by the Russian Federation in its war of aggression against Ukraine”.
Investigations into drones shot down on Saturday and Sunday continued, he said.
“It is unacceptable and intolerable for the Russian Federation to continue violating Romania’s airspace, which is also the airspace of Nato and the European Union,” Dan said on X.
The drone shot down on Sunday also appeared to be of “Russian origin”, Martin O’Donnell, a senior Nato military spokesperson, said.
He said the downing of the drones came as Romania and other Nato countries were actively acquiring “ground-based interceptors” to increase their air defences.
Romania integrated the US-made Merops counter-drone system into its defences at the end of June. AI-powered, the mobile system is designed to intercept small targets flying at low altitudes.
The country has reported dozens of drone incursions since the start of the Ukraine war. One smashed into a residential building in Galați on the border with Ukraine in May, wounding two people.
Romania’s parliament adopted a law in 2025 allowing drones that breach its airspace to be shot down.
Several countries near the Ukraine conflict have shot down drones since the war started.

title: Carrie is just trying to make a friend in the new trailer

full_text:
Mike Flanagan’s latest Stephen King adaptation, Carrie (this will be his fourth), is slated to make its debut on Amazon Prime on October 7th. The new trailer dropped at Comic-Con 2026 and doesn’t contain many surprises. If you’re familiar with Carrie at all, it hits all the expected notes. Though it’s clearly been updated for the modern era.
Carrie is just trying to make a friend in the new trailer
Mike Flanagan’s adaptation updates the Stephen King classic for the modern age.
Mike Flanagan’s adaptation updates the Stephen King classic for the modern age.
According to Deadline, Flanagan’s take on the classic King novel will tackle very modern teen challenges like active shooter drills and bullying on social media. The director apparently invited high schoolers into the writers’ room, using their real-life traumas to inform the script:
“They shared shocking one-off situations or constant treatment and microaggressions and things that are not necessarily present themselves as targeted harassment. [We will dive into] the cruelty in today’s world and how the internet has encouraged cruelty, rewards and celebrates and amplifies it. This is awful for adults to deal with, and for teenagers even more so.”
Brian De Palma’s iconic 1976 adaptation of Carrie is iconic and features an unimpeachable performance from Sissy Spacek. But it’s undeniable that Summer H. Howell, who was 21 at the time of shooting, is much more believable as a high school student than Spacek, who was 26 at the time.

full_text:
Subscribing to Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on a recurring basis has been tough to justify recently, even after Microsoft reduced the monthly cost from $29.99 to $22.99. But you can get a better deal on a three-month subscription (valued at $69) by grabbing a digital code at Eneba that costs $39.01 at the time of publication.
You can get three months of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate for almost half off
Jump into Halo: Campaign Evolved and many other great games for significantly less than the normal monthly cost.
Jump into Halo: Campaign Evolved and many other great games for significantly less than the normal monthly cost.
Game Pass Ultimate grants you access to the full Game Pass library on Xbox (compared to a more limited slice with Premium), including first-party titles and online multiplayer access. The subscription also gives PC gamers access to Microsoft’s catalog of Game Pass games through the Xbox app, though the selection differs a bit between console and desktop.
You don’t need me to tell you why deals like these are nice. The costs of subscriptions generally only go in one direction over time, and it is becoming more rare to find worthwhile discounts that give you a break. If you want to jump into Halo: Campaign Evolved when it launches July 28th on Xbox and PC, all you need is this subscription instead of buying the $49.99 re-remake.

full_text:
While perhaps less dramatic than in years past, Marvel nonetheless had some big reveals lined up for Comic-Con. The highest profile was certainly the announcement that Ryan Gosling would be joining the MCU as Ghost Rider, with the Shawn Levy-directed (Deadpool & Wolverine) standalone feature set to drop sometime in 2028.
Marvel announces Ryan Gosling as Ghost Rider, a new Black Panther, and more
Black Panther III will land on December 15th, 2028.
Black Panther III will land on December 15th, 2028.
The studio also brought out Ryan Coogler, who officially confirmed Black Panther III is slated for release on December 15th, 2028. He also introduced David Jonsson (The Long Walk, Alien Romulus) as T’Chala’s son and the new Black Panther in the franchise.
Marvel also showed off a new Avengers: Doomsday trailer and seemed to reveal yet another cast member. Ryan Reynolds made an appearance in the crowd as Deadpool and stood up to ask the film’s directors, Joe and Anthony Russo, if there was room for him in the movie. They said the film was basically done, but they might be able to work something out. It was also confirmed that Hayley Atwell is returning as Peggy Carter.
